title.zh: 卷一百七十六 列傳第六十四 李賢 呂原 岳正 彭時 商輅 劉定之
title.en: Volume 176 Biographies 64: Li Xian, Lu Yuan, Yue Zheng, Peng Shi, Shang Lu, Liu Dingzhi
title.raw: 卷一百七十六 列傳第六十四 李賢 呂原 岳正 彭時 商輅 劉定之 Volume 176 Biographies 64: Li Xian, Lu Yuan, Yue Zheng, Peng Shi, Shang Lu, Liu Dingzhi

sentences.zh: 李賢呂原

translations.literal: Li Xian, Lu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian and Lu Yuan.

translations.literal: (Zi Chang)⟩〉
translations.idiomatic: (style name Zi Chang)⟩〉

sentences.zh: 嶽正彭時商輅劉定之

translations.literal: Yue Zheng, Peng Shi, Shang Lu, Liu Dingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Zheng, Peng Shi, Shang Lu, and Liu Dingzhi.

sentences.zh: 李賢，字原德，鄧人。

translations.literal: Li Xian, style name Yuande, was a native of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, styled Yuande, was from Deng.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試第一，宣德八年成進士。

translations.literal: He took first place in the provincial examination and became a jinshi in the eighth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in the provincial examinations and passed the palace examination as a jinshi in the eighth year of the Xuande reign (1433).

sentences.zh: 奉命察蝗災於河津，授驗封主事，少師楊士奇欲一見，賢竟不往。

translations.literal: Ordered to investigate locust disasters at Hejin, he was appointed principal secretary of Yanfeng; the Senior Preceptor Yang Shiqi wished to meet him once, but Xian did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When sent to inspect locust damage at Hejin, he was appointed principal secretary in the Yanfeng department. The Senior Preceptor Yang Shiqi wished to meet him, but Xian declined to call on him.

sentences.zh: 正統初，言：「塞外降人居京師者盈萬，指揮使月俸三十五石，實支僅一石，降人反實支十七石五鬥，是一降人當京官十七員半矣。

translations.literal: In the early Zhengtong period he memorialized: Those who surrendered from beyond the frontier and dwell in the capital exceed ten thousand. A commander receives thirty-five shi per month in salary, but only one shi is actually paid, while a surrendered person actually receives seventeen shi and five dou — one surrendered person equals seventeen and a half capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengtong reign he memorialized: More than ten thousand people who had surrendered from beyond the border were living in the capital. A commander nominally drew thirty-five shi of grain per month but actually received only one, whereas a surrendered tribesman actually received seventeen shi and five dou — so one surrendered person consumed as much as seventeen and a half capital officials.

sentences.zh: 宜漸出之外，省冗費，且消患未萌。」

translations.literal: They should gradually be moved outside, to reduce redundant expense and to eliminate trouble before it arises.
translations.idiomatic: They ought gradually to be resettled outside the capital, both to cut waste and to snuff out trouble before it could take root.

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept his proposal.

sentences.zh: 時詔文武臣誥敕，非九年不給。

translations.literal: At that time it was decreed that patent letters of appointment for civil and military officials would not be issued unless after nine years of service.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then stipulated that civil and military officials would not receive patent letters of appointment until they had served nine years.

sentences.zh: 賢言：「限以九年，或官不能滿秩，或親老不待，不得者十八九，無以勸臣下。

translations.literal: Xian said: If limited to nine years, some officials cannot complete a full term, and some have aged parents who cannot wait — eighteen or nineteen out of ten do not receive them, and there is no way to encourage subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Xian argued: With a nine-year requirement, some officials never complete a full term of office, and others have elderly parents who cannot wait that long — eight or nine out of ten never receive their patents, so there is no incentive for officials to serve diligently.

sentences.zh: 請仍三年便。」

translations.literal: He requested that three years again be sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the three-year interval be restored.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷考功郎中，改文選。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be director in the Bureau of Appointments and then moved to the Bureau of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Bureau of Appointments and then transferred to the Bureau of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 扈從北征，師覆脫還。

translations.literal: He accompanied the northern expedition; the army was destroyed, but he escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the northern campaign; when the army was annihilated, he escaped and made his way back.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年二月上正本十策，曰勤聖學，顧箴警，戒嗜欲，絕玩好，慎舉措，崇節儉，畏天變，勉貴近，振士風，結民心。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Jingtai he submitted ten fundamental policies: diligent imperial study, heedful admonition and warning, restraint from indulgence, rejection of frivolities, careful conduct, esteem for frugality, reverence for heavenly portents, encouragement of the nobility and those near the throne, revival of scholarly conduct, and winning the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Jingtai (1451), he presented ten fundamental policies: cultivate the emperor's learning, heed admonitions and warnings, guard against indulgence, renounce frivolous pursuits, act with care, uphold frugality, revere heavenly portents, encourage the nobility and those close to the throne, revive scholarly standards, and bind the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，命翰林寫置左右，備省覽。

translations.literal: The emperor approved them and ordered the Hanlin Academy to copy them and place them at hand for review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved them and had the Hanlin Academy copy them out to keep at his side for regular consultation.

sentences.zh: 尋又陳車戰火器之利，帝頗采納。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also set forth the advantages of chariot warfare and firearms, and the emperor largely adopted his suggestions.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed with a memorial on the advantages of chariot warfare and firearms, and the emperor largely accepted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 是冬，擢兵部右侍郎，轉戶部。

translations.literal: That winter he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and then moved to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 也先數貢馬，賢謂輦金帛以強寇自弊，非策。

translations.literal: Esen repeatedly presented tribute horses; Xian said that conveying gold and silks to strengthen a powerful foe was self-defeating and not a sound policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen repeatedly sent tribute horses, Xian argued that shipping gold and silk to enrich a powerful enemy was self-defeating and no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 因陳邊備廢馳狀，于謙請下其章厲諸將。

translations.literal: He then described the neglected state of frontier defenses; Yu Qian requested that his memorial be circulated to rouse the generals.
translations.idiomatic: He also described how frontier defenses had fallen into neglect, and Yu Qian asked that his memorial be distributed to spur the generals to action.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部，采古二十二君行事可法者。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he collected the conduct of twenty-two ancient rulers that could serve as models.
translations.idiomatic: After his transfer to the Ministry of Personnel, he compiled the exemplary deeds of twenty-two ancient rulers.

sentences.zh: 曰《鑒古錄》，上之。

translations.literal: Entitled Mirror of Antiquity, he submitted it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He titled the work Mirror of Antiquity and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，命兼翰林學士，入直文淵閣，與徐有貞同預機務。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, Xian was appointed concurrently as Hanlin Academician, entered attendance at the Wenyuan Pavilion, and together with Xu Youzhen shared in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Xian was appointed concurrent Hanlin Academician, took up duty in the Wenyuan Pavilion, and joined Xu Youzhen in managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 賢氣度端凝，奏對皆中機宜，帝深眷之。

translations.literal: Xian's bearing was dignified and composed; his memorials and responses all hit the mark, and the emperor deeply favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian carried himself with dignified composure; his memorials and replies always struck the right note, and the emperor held him in deep regard.

sentences.zh: 山東饑，發帑振不足，召有貞及賢議，有貞謂頒振多中飽。

translations.literal: When Shandong suffered famine, treasury funds for relief were insufficient; the emperor summoned Xu Youzhen and Xian to discuss it, and Youzhen said that distributing relief often led to embezzlement en route.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Shandong and treasury funds for relief proved insufficient, the emperor summoned Xu Youzhen and Xian to discuss the matter. Youzhen argued that distributing relief grain invited widespread embezzlement along the way.

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「慮中飽而不貸，坐視民死，是因噎廢食也。」

translations.literal: Xian said: To fear embezzlement and withhold aid, sitting by while the people die — that is to choke and abandon eating altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied: To fear embezzlement and withhold relief while watching the people starve is like refusing to eat for fear of choking.

sentences.zh: 遂命增銀。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered additional silver to be allocated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered additional silver to be disbursed.

sentences.zh: 石亨、曹吉祥與有貞爭權，並忌賢。

translations.literal: Shi Heng, Cao Jixiang, and Xu Youzhen struggled for power, and all resented Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng and Cao Jixiang were locked in a power struggle with Xu Youzhen, and they all resented Xian as well.

sentences.zh: 諸御史論亨、吉祥，亨、吉祥疑出有貞、賢意，訴之帝，下二人獄。

translations.literal: When censors impeached Heng and Jixiang, Heng and Jixiang suspected the move came from Youzhen and Xian; they complained to the emperor, and both men were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When censors impeached Heng and Jixiang, the two men suspected the move had been instigated by Youzhen and Xian. They appealed to the emperor, and both Youzhen and Xian were thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 會有風雷變，得釋，謫賢福建參政。

translations.literal: When wind and thunder portents occurred, they were released; Xian was demoted to administrative commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: When wind and thunder portents appeared, they were released, but Xian was demoted to administrative commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 未行，王翺奏賢可大用，遂留為吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Before he departed, Wang Ao memorialized that Xian could be greatly employed, and so he was retained as Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, Wang Ao memorialized that Xian was fit for greater responsibility, and he was kept on as Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 逾月，復尚書，直內閣如故。

translations.literal: After a month he was restored to Minister and continued in the Grand Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was restored to ministerial rank and resumed his duties in the Grand Secretariat as before.

sentences.zh: 亨知帝向賢，怒，然無可如何，乃佯與交歡。

translations.literal: Heng knew the emperor favored Xian and was angry, but could do nothing about it; he therefore feigned cordiality.
translations.idiomatic: Heng knew the emperor favored Xian and was furious, but could do nothing about it, so he pretended to be on friendly terms.

sentences.zh: 賢亦深自匿，非宣召不入，而帝益親賢，顧問無虛日。

translations.literal: Xian also kept himself deeply concealed, entering only when summoned, yet the emperor grew still closer to him and consulted him without missing a day.
translations.idiomatic: Xian likewise kept a low profile, entering the palace only when summoned, yet the emperor drew even closer to him and sought his counsel nearly every day.

sentences.zh: 孛來近塞獵。

translations.literal: Bolai hunted near the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Bolai came to hunt near the border.

sentences.zh: 亨言傳國璽在彼，可掩而取，帝色動。

translations.literal: Heng said the dynastic seal was there and could be seized in a surprise attack; the emperor's expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: Heng reported that the dynastic seal was in Bolai's camp and could be seized in a surprise attack; the emperor's expression changed at once.

sentences.zh: 賢言釁不可啟，璽不足寶，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Xian said that provocation must not be invited and the seal was not worth treasuring; the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Xian argued that provocation must not be invited and that the seal was not worth the risk; the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 亨益惡賢。

translations.literal: Heng hated Xian all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Heng came to hate Xian even more.

sentences.zh: 時帝亦厭亨、吉祥驕橫，屏人語賢曰：「此輩幹政，四方奏事者先至其門，為之奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor also grew weary of Heng and Jixiang's arrogance; dismissing attendants, he said to Xian: These men interfere in government — memorialists from all quarters reach their doors first. What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had also grown weary of Heng and Jixiang's arrogance. Sending attendants away, he said to Xian: "These men meddle in government affairs — petitioners from every province reach their doors before mine. What can be done about this?

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「陛下惟獨斷，則趨附自息。」

translations.literal: Xian said: If Your Majesty decides matters independently, the rush to attach will cease of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied: "If Your Majesty decides matters on your own authority, the rush to curry favor will die down of itself."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「向嘗不用其言，乃怫然見辭色。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: When I have not followed their advice, they show displeasure in word and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Whenever I have rejected their advice, they show open displeasure in word and expression."

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「願制之以漸。」

translations.literal: Xian said: I hope Your Majesty will restrain them gradually.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said: "I hope Your Majesty will restrain them step by step."

sentences.zh: 當亨、吉祥用事，賢顧忌不敢盡言，然每從容論對，所以裁抑之者甚至。

translations.literal: While Heng and Jixiang held power, Xian was cautious and did not dare speak fully, yet in each calm exchange he restrained them to a considerable degree.
translations.idiomatic: While Heng and Jixiang held power, Xian held back and did not speak as freely as he wished, yet in each measured exchange he managed to check their influence considerably.

sentences.zh: 及亨得罪，帝復問賢「奪門」事。

translations.literal: When Heng fell from grace, the emperor again asked Xian about the "Seizing the Gate" affair.
translations.idiomatic: After Heng fell from power, the emperor again questioned Xian about the "Seizing the Gate" affair.

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「『迎駕』則可，『奪門』豈可示後？

translations.literal: Xian said: "Welcoming the Imperial Carriage" would have been acceptable — how could "Seizing the Gate" be held up as an example for posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Xian said: "'Welcoming the Imperial Carriage' would have been acceptable — but how could 'Seizing the Gate' be held up as an example for posterity?

sentences.zh: 天位乃陛下固有，『奪』即非順。

translations.literal: The throne was inherently Your Majesty's; to "seize" it was not in accord with propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was inherently yours, Your Majesty — to "seize" it was not the proper course.

sentences.zh: 且爾時幸而成功，萬一事機先露，亨等不足惜，不審置陛下何地！」

translations.literal: Moreover, though it succeeded by good fortune at the time, had the plan been exposed beforehand, Heng and the others would not have mattered — but where would Your Majesty have been placed!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though the plot succeeded by good fortune at the time, had it been exposed beforehand, Heng and his followers would have been expendable — but where would that have left Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 帝悟曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The emperor understood and said: So it is.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the point and said: "True enough."

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「若郕王果不起，群臣表請陛下復位，安用擾攘為？

translations.literal: Xian said: If the Prince of Cheng had truly not recovered, the officials would have petitioned for Your Majesty's restoration — why need there have been such turmoil?
translations.idiomatic: Xian continued: "If the Prince of Cheng had truly not recovered, the officials would simply have petitioned for Your Majesty's restoration — why was all that turmoil necessary?

sentences.zh: 此輩又安所得邀升賞，招權納賄安自起？

translations.literal: How could these men then have claimed promotions and rewards, or how could the solicitation of power and bribes have arisen?
translations.idiomatic: How then could these men have claimed promotions and rewards, or how could the abuse of power and acceptance of bribes have taken root?

sentences.zh: 老成耆舊依然在職，何至有殺戮降黜之事致幹天象？

translations.literal: Experienced elders would still have held office — how could there have been killings and demotions provoking heavenly signs?
translations.idiomatic: Experienced elders would still have held their posts — how could there have been killings and demotions that provoked portents in the heavens?

sentences.zh: 《易》曰『開國承家，小人勿用』，正謂此也。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says, "In founding a state and sustaining a household, petty men must not be employed" — it speaks precisely of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "In founding a state and sustaining a household, petty men must not be employed" — it speaks precisely to this."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: So it is.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "True."

sentences.zh: 詔自今章奏勿用「奪門」字，並議革冒功者四千余人。

translations.literal: An edict declared that from then on memorials must not use the term "Seizing the Gate," and more than four thousand who had falsely claimed merit were considered for removal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that from then on memorials must not use the term "Seizing the Gate," and more than four thousand men who had falsely claimed merit were marked for removal.

sentences.zh: 至成化初，諸被革者訴請。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, those who had been removed petitioned for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chenghua reign, those who had been stripped of honors petitioned for restoration.

sentences.zh: 復以賢言，並奪太平侯張瑾、興濟伯楊宗爵，時論益大快之。

translations.literal: Again following Xian's advice, the titles of Marquis of Taiping Zhang Jin and Earl of Xingji Yang Zong were also revoked; public opinion was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Again heeding Xian's counsel, the titles of Marquis of Taiping Zhang Jin and Earl of Xingji Yang Zong were also revoked, to widespread public approval.

sentences.zh: 帝既任賢，所言皆見聽。

translations.literal: Once the emperor entrusted affairs to Xian, whatever he said was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor entrusted affairs to Xian, his counsel was invariably heeded.

sentences.zh: 于謙嘗分遣降人南征，陳汝言希宦官指，盡召之還。

translations.literal: Yu Qian had once dispatched surrendered tribesmen on southern campaigns; Chen Ruyan, currying favor with eunuchs, recalled them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian had once dispatched surrendered tribesmen on southern campaigns, but Chen Ruyan, currying favor with the eunuchs, recalled them all.

sentences.zh: 賢力言不可。

translations.literal: Xian strongly argued that this must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Xian strongly argued against it.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾亦悔之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: I also regret it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I regret it too.

sentences.zh: 今已就道，後當聽其願去者。」

translations.literal: They are already on the road; hereafter those who wish to leave should be allowed to do so.
translations.idiomatic: They are already on the march; hereafter those who wish to leave should be permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 帝憂軍官支俸多，歲入不給。

translations.literal: The emperor worried that military officers' salaries were too heavy and annual revenue could not cover them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried that military officers' salaries consumed too much and that annual revenue could not cover the expense.

sentences.zh: 賢請汰老弱於外，則費省而人不覺。

translations.literal: Xian requested that the aged and weak be weeded out on the frontiers, so expense would be saved without people noticing.
translations.idiomatic: Xian proposed weeding out the aged and infirm on the frontiers, so costs would be cut without anyone feeling the loss.

sentences.zh: 帝深納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the proposal wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 時歲有邊警，天下大水，江南北尤甚。

translations.literal: At the time there were frontier alarms each year, and great floods throughout the realm, especially severe south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: At the time frontier alarms came every year, and great floods swept the empire, with the region south of the Yangzi hit hardest.

sentences.zh: 賢外籌邊計，內請寬百姓，罷一切征求。

translations.literal: Xian planned frontier strategy abroad and within requested relief for the people and the abolition of all levies.
translations.idiomatic: Xian devised frontier strategy while pressing within for relief for the people and the abolition of all exactions.

sentences.zh: 帝用其言，四方得蘇息。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted his advice, and the four quarters found respite.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted his counsel, and the realm found respite.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，空中有聲，帝欲禳之，命賢撰青詞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, sounds were heard in the sky; the emperor wished to perform rites of expiation and ordered Xian to compose the green-ink prayer.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year, strange sounds were heard in the sky; the emperor wished to perform expiatory rites and ordered Xian to compose the ceremonial prayer text.

sentences.zh: 賢言君不恤民，天下怨叛，厥有鼓妖。

translations.literal: Xian said that when the ruler does not care for the people, the realm resents and rebels, and there arise drum-like portents.
translations.idiomatic: Xian argued that when a ruler neglects the people, the realm turns resentful and rebellious, and portents such as these arise.

sentences.zh: 因請行寬恤之政，又請罷江南織造，清錦衣獄，止邊臣貢獻，停內外采買。

translations.literal: He therefore requested lenient and compassionate policies, and also asked to abolish Jiangnan weaving offices, clear cases in the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison, stop frontier officials' tribute offerings, and halt purchases inside and outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore pressed for lenient and compassionate policies, and also asked to abolish the Jiangnan weaving offices, clear cases in the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison, halt tribute offerings from frontier officials, and stop procurement inside and outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝難之。

translations.literal: The emperor found it difficult to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor balked at these proposals.

sentences.zh: 賢執爭數四，同列皆懼。

translations.literal: Xian argued persistently four times; his colleagues were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Xian pressed his case four times over; his colleagues were all alarmed.

sentences.zh: 賢退曰：「大臣當知無不言，可卷舌偷位耶？」

translations.literal: Xian withdrew and said: A grand minister should speak without holding back — can one roll up one's tongue and steal one's office?
translations.idiomatic: On leaving, Xian said: "A grand minister should speak without holding back — can one hold one's tongue and cling to office?

sentences.zh: 終天順之世，賢為首輔，呂原、彭時佐之，然賢委任最專。

translations.literal: Throughout the Tianshun reign, Xian was chief minister, with Lu Yuan and Peng Shi assisting, yet Xian's commission was the most exclusive.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Tianshun reign, Xian served as chief minister, assisted by Lu Yuan and Peng Shi, but he held the broadest authority of the three.

sentences.zh: 初，御史劉濬劾柳溥敗軍罪，觸帝怒。

translations.literal: Initially, Censor Liu Jun impeached Liu Pu for defeat in battle, provoking the emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Censor Liu Jun impeached Liu Pu for military defeat, provoking the emperor's wrath.

sentences.zh: 賢言御史耳目官，不宜譴。

translations.literal: Xian said that censors are the eyes and ears of the court and should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xian argued that censors serve as the court's eyes and ears and should not be punished for doing their duty.

sentences.zh: 石亨譖賢曲護。

translations.literal: Shi Heng slandered Xian for partial protection.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng slandered Xian for showing partiality.

sentences.zh: 帝浸疏賢，尋悟，待之如初。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually grew distant from Xian, but soon realized his error and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gradually grew cool toward Xian, but soon saw his error and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 每獨對，良久方出。

translations.literal: Each time they met alone, he remained a long while before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they met in private audience, the sessions ran long before Xian withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遇事必召問可否，或遣中官就問。

translations.literal: When affairs arose he always summoned Xian to ask his view, or sent a eunuch to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever affairs arose, the emperor summoned Xian to ask his opinion, or sent a eunuch to consult him.

sentences.zh: 賢務持大體，尤以惜人才、開言路為急。

translations.literal: Xian strove to uphold the larger principles, especially cherishing talent and opening avenues of speech as urgent priorities.
translations.idiomatic: Xian held fast to the larger principles, above all cherishing talent and keeping channels of candid speech open.

sentences.zh: 所薦引年富、軒輗、耿九疇、王竑、李秉、程信、姚夔、崔恭、李紹等，皆為名臣。

translations.literal: Those he recommended and advanced — Nian Fu, Xuan Ni, Geng Jiuchou, Wang Hong, Li Bing, Cheng Xin, Yao Kui, Cui Gong, Li Shao, and others — all became renowned ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Those he recommended and advanced — Nian Fu, Xuan Ni, Geng Jiuchou, Wang Hong, Li Bing, Cheng Xin, Yao Kui, Cui Gong, Li Shao, and others — all became celebrated ministers.

sentences.zh: 時勸帝延見大臣，有所薦，必先與吏、兵二部論定之。

translations.literal: He often urged the emperor to receive ministers in audience; when making recommendations, he always discussed and settled them first with the Ministries of Personnel and War.
translations.idiomatic: He often urged the emperor to receive ministers in audience, and whenever he made a recommendation, he first settled the matter with the Ministries of Personnel and War.

sentences.zh: 及入對，帝訪文臣，請問王翺；

translations.literal: When entering audience, if the emperor inquired about civil officials, he would ask about Wang Ao;
translations.idiomatic: When entering audience, if the emperor asked about civil officials, Xian would consult Wang Ao;

sentences.zh: 武臣，請問馬昂。

translations.literal: for military officials, he would ask about Ma Ang.
translations.idiomatic: for military officials, he would consult Ma Ang.

sentences.zh: 兩人相左右，故言無不行，而人不病其專，惟群小與為難。

translations.literal: The two men supported him on either side, so his words were never unheeded, yet people did not fault his exclusiveness — only petty men made trouble with him.
translations.idiomatic: With these two men supporting him, his recommendations were invariably adopted, yet no one faulted him for overreach — only petty men made trouble with him.

sentences.zh: 曹欽之反也，擊賢東朝房，執將殺之，逼草奏釋己罪。

translations.literal: When Cao Qin rebelled, he attacked Xian in the Eastern Court chamber, seized him intending to kill him, and forced him to draft a memorial absolving his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Qin rebelled, his men stormed Xian's chamber in the Eastern Court, seized him intending to kill him, and forced him to draft a memorial absolving Qin of guilt.

sentences.zh: 賴王翺救，乃免。

translations.literal: Thanks to Wang Ao's rescue, he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao rescued him, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 賢密疏請擒賊黨。

translations.literal: Xian sent a secret memorial requesting the capture of the rebel faction.
translations.idiomatic: Xian sent a secret memorial urging the capture of the rebel faction.

sentences.zh: 時方擾攘，不知賢所在。

translations.literal: At the time turmoil reigned and no one knew where Xian was.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the turmoil, no one knew where Xian was.

sentences.zh: 得疏，帝大喜。

translations.literal: Receiving the memorial, the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, the emperor was greatly relieved.

sentences.zh: 裹傷入見，慰勞之，特加太子太保。

translations.literal: Bandaged, he entered audience; the emperor consoled and commended him and specially added the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Bandaged, he came before the emperor, who consoled and commended him and specially granted him the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 賢因言，賊既誅，急宜詔天下停不急務，而求直言以通閉塞。

translations.literal: Xian then said that once the rebels were executed, an urgent edict should announce to the realm the suspension of nonessential affairs and seek forthright speech to open blocked channels.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then urged that once the rebels were executed, an urgent edict should announce the suspension of nonessential affairs throughout the realm and invite forthright speech to unblock stifled channels of communication.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 門達方用事，錦衣官校恣橫為劇患。

translations.literal: Men Da was then in power, and Embroidered Uniform Guard officers ran rampant as a grave affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Men Da was then in power, and the rampant abuse of authority by Embroidered Uniform Guard officers had become a grave affliction.

sentences.zh: 賢累請禁止，帝召達誡諭之。

translations.literal: Xian repeatedly requested prohibition; the emperor summoned Da and admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian repeatedly petitioned for a ban on such abuses; the emperor summoned Da and admonished him.

sentences.zh: 達怙寵益驕，賢乘間復具陳達罪，帝復召戒達。

translations.literal: Da, relying on favor, grew still more arrogant; Xian seized an opportunity to set forth Da's crimes in full, and the emperor again summoned and warned Da.
translations.idiomatic: Da, emboldened by imperial favor, grew still more arrogant; Xian seized an opportunity to lay out Da's crimes in full, and the emperor summoned and warned him again.

sentences.zh: 達銜次骨，因袁彬獄陷賢，賢幾不免，語載達傳。

translations.literal: Da bore a grudge to the bone; through the Yuan Bin case he framed Xian, who nearly perished — the account is given in Da's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Da nursed a grudge to the bone; through the Yuan Bin case he framed Xian, who nearly perished — the full account appears in Da's biography.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，臥文華殿。

translations.literal: The emperor was unwell and lay ill in the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, he took to his bed in the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 會有間東宮於帝者，帝頗惑之，密告賢。

translations.literal: Someone sowed discord about the Eastern Palace with the emperor; the emperor was somewhat swayed and secretly told Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Someone sowed discord about the crown prince with the emperor; the emperor was somewhat swayed and confided in Xian in secret.

sentences.zh: 賢頓首伏地曰：「此大事，願陛下三思。」

translations.literal: Xian kowtowed and prostrated himself, saying: This is a grave matter; I hope Your Majesty will think thrice.
translations.idiomatic: Xian kowtowed and prostrated himself, saying: "This is a grave matter — I beg Your Majesty to think it through carefully.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然則必傳位太子乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: Then must the throne be passed to the crown prince?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Then must the throne be passed to the crown prince?"

sentences.zh: 賢又頓首曰：「宗社幸甚。」

translations.literal: Xian again kowtowed and said: The altars of state would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: Xian kowtowed again and said: "The altars of state would be greatly blessed."

sentences.zh: 帝起，立召太子至。

translations.literal: The emperor rose and immediately summoned the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose at once and summoned the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 賢扶太子令謝。

translations.literal: Xian supported the crown prince and had him give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Xian steadied the crown prince and had him offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 太子謝，抱帝足泣，帝亦泣，讒竟不行。

translations.literal: The crown prince gave thanks, embraced the emperor's feet and wept; the emperor wept as well, and the slander came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince gave thanks, clung to the emperor's feet and wept; the emperor wept as well, and the slander came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 門達既竄，其黨多投匿名書構賢。

translations.literal: After Men Da fled, many of his faction submitted anonymous letters to frame Xian.
translations.idiomatic: After Men Da fled into exile, many of his followers submitted anonymous letters to frame Xian.

sentences.zh: 賢乞罷，有詔慰留。

translations.literal: Xian requested dismissal; an edict consoled him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Xian asked to resign; an edict consoled him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 吳後廢，言官請誅牛玉，語侵賢，又有造蜚語構賢者。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu was deposed, censors called for the execution of Niu Yu, with words impugning Xian; there were also those who spread slander to frame him.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu was deposed, censors called for the execution of Niu Yu in language that impugned Xian as well, and others spread slander to frame him.

sentences.zh: 帝命衛士宿賢家，護出入。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered guards to lodge at Xian's home to protect his comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered guards to lodge at Xian's home to protect him when he went out and returned.

sentences.zh: 成化二年三月遭父喪，詔起復。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Chenghua he suffered his father's death; an edict recalled him from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Chenghua (1466), he suffered his father's death; an edict ordered him recalled from mourning.

sentences.zh: 三辭不許，遣中官護行營葬。

translations.literal: He declined three times but was not permitted; a eunuch was sent to escort him and oversee the burial.
translations.idiomatic: He declined three times but was not permitted; a eunuch was dispatched to escort him and oversee the burial.

sentences.zh: 還至京，又辭。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he declined again.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital, he declined again.

sentences.zh: 遣使宣意，遂視事。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to convey the emperor's intent, and he then resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to convey the emperor's wishes, and he resumed his duties.

sentences.zh: 其年冬卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: That winter he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died that winter at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝震悼，贈太師，謚文達。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply shaken and grieved; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Wendá.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply shaken and grieved; Xian was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Wendá.

sentences.zh: 賢自以受知人主，所言無不盡。

translations.literal: Xian considered himself known and trusted by his sovereign, and spoke without holding back.
translations.idiomatic: Xian considered himself known and trusted by his sovereign, and held nothing back in his counsel.

sentences.zh: 景帝崩，將以汪後殉葬，用賢言而止。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing died, Empress Wang was to be buried alive with him; on Xian's advice this was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing died, Empress Wang was to be buried alive with him; on Xian's advice the practice was halted.

sentences.zh: 惠帝少子幽禁已六十年，英宗憐欲赦之，以問賢。

translations.literal: The youngest son of Emperor Hui had been confined for sixty years; Emperor Yingzong pitied him and wished to pardon him, and asked Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son of Emperor Hui had been confined for sixty years; Emperor Yingzong pitied him and wished to pardon him, and consulted Xian.

sentences.zh: 賢頓首曰：「此堯、舜用心也！

translations.literal: Xian kowtowed and said: This is the heart of Yao and Shun!
translations.idiomatic: Xian kowtowed and said: "This is the heart of Yao and Shun!

sentences.zh: 天地祖宗實式憑之。」

translations.literal: Heaven, earth, and the imperial ancestors will truly rely upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, earth, and the imperial ancestors will truly approve.

sentences.zh: 帝意乃決。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗祭山川壇，以夜出未便，欲遣官代祀。

translations.literal: The emperor once was to sacrifice at the altars of mountains and rivers; because going out at night was inconvenient, he wished to send an official to sacrifice in his place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once was to sacrifice at the altars of mountains and rivers; because going out at night was inconvenient, he wished to send an official to perform the rites in his stead.

sentences.zh: 賢引祖訓爭之，卒成禮而還。

translations.literal: Xian cited the ancestral injunctions and argued against it; in the end the rites were completed and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xian cited the ancestral injunctions and argued against it; in the end the emperor completed the rites himself and returned.

sentences.zh: 嘗言內帑余財，不以恤荒濟軍，則人主必生侈心，而移之於土木禱祠聲色之用。

translations.literal: He once said that surplus funds in the inner treasury, if not used to relieve famine and support the army, would surely breed extravagance in the ruler and shift spending to construction, prayer shrines, and pleasures.
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that surplus funds in the inner treasury, if not used to relieve famine and support the army, would surely breed extravagance in the ruler and divert spending toward construction projects, prayer shrines, and sensual indulgence.

sentences.zh: 前後頻請發帑振貸恤邊，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Before and after he repeatedly requested treasury disbursements for relief, loans, and frontier aid — too many to count.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again he petitioned for treasury disbursements for famine relief, loans, and frontier aid — too many to count.

sentences.zh: 故事，方面官敕三品京官保舉。

translations.literal: By precedent, provincial appointments required recommendation by capital officials of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, appointments to provincial posts required recommendation by capital officials of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 賢患其營競，令吏部每缺舉二人，請帝簡用。

translations.literal: Xian worried about the scramble for favor; he ordered the Ministry of Personnel to nominate two candidates for each vacancy and asked the emperor to choose.
translations.idiomatic: Xian worried about the scramble for favor; he ordered the Ministry of Personnel to nominate two candidates for each vacancy and asked the emperor to choose between them.

sentences.zh: 並推之例始此。

translations.literal: The practice of joint nomination began here.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of joint nomination began with this reform.

sentences.zh: 自三楊以來，得君無如賢者。

translations.literal: Since the Three Yangs, none had won the sovereign's trust like Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Since the era of the Three Yangs, no minister had won the sovereign's trust like Xian.

sentences.zh: 然自郎署結知景帝，超擢侍郎，而所著書顧謂景帝為荒淫。

translations.literal: Yet from his post in the secretariat he won Emperor Jing's favor and was abruptly promoted to vice minister, while in his writings he nevertheless called Emperor Jing dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from a lowly secretariat post he had won Emperor Jing's favor and been abruptly promoted to vice minister, while in his writings he nevertheless called Emperor Jing dissolute.

sentences.zh: 其抑葉盛，擠嶽正，不救羅倫，尤為世所惜雲。

translations.literal: His suppression of Ye Sheng, his squeezing out of Yue Zheng, and his failure to save Luo Lun were especially regretted by the world.
translations.idiomatic: His suppression of Ye Sheng, his squeezing out of Yue Zheng, and his failure to save Luo Lun were especially regretted by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 呂原，字逢原，秀水人。

translations.literal: Lu Yuan, style name Fengyuan, was a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan, styled Fengyuan, was from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 父嗣芳，萬泉教諭。

translations.literal: His father Sifang was instructor at Wanquan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sifang served as instructor at Wanquan.

sentences.zh: 兄本，景州訓導。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ben was assistant instructor at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ben served as assistant instructor at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗣芳老，就養景州，與本相繼卒。

translations.literal: When Sifang grew old, he went to Jingzhou to be supported and died there, followed in death by Ben.
translations.idiomatic: When Sifang grew old, he went to Jingzhou to live with Ben and died there; Ben followed him in death soon after.

sentences.zh: 貧不能歸葬，厝於景，原時至墓慟哭。

translations.literal: Too poor to return them for burial, he placed them in temporary interment at Jing; Yuan often came to the graves and wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to return them home for burial, he placed them in temporary interment at Jing; Yuan often visited the graves and wept in grief.

sentences.zh: 久之，奉母南歸，家益貧。

translations.literal: After a long time he escorted his mother south to return home, and the family grew still poorer.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he escorted his mother south to return home, and the family grew still poorer.

sentences.zh: 知府黃懋奇原文，補諸生，遣入學，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: Prefect Huang Maoqi admired Yuan, enrolled him as a student, sent him to study, and he took first place in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Huang Maoqi admired Yuan, enrolled him as a student and sent him to study; Yuan ranked first in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 正統七年，進士及第，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengtong he passed the palace examination as a jinshi and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhengtong (1442), he passed the palace examination as a jinshi and was appointed a compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 十二年，與侍講裴綸等十人同選入東閣肄業，直經筵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he and ten others including Reader-in-Waiting Pei Lun were selected to study in the Eastern Pavilion and attend the Classics Lectern.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1447), he and ten others including Reader-in-Waiting Pei Lun were selected to study in the Eastern Pavilion and attend the Classics Lectern.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，進侍講，與同官倪謙授小內侍書於文華殿東廡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting and, with his colleague Ni Qian, taught young inner eunuchs to write in the eastern corridor of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingtai reign he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting and, with his colleague Ni Qian, taught young inner eunuchs to write in the eastern corridor of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝至，命謙講《國風》。

translations.literal: When the emperor arrived, he ordered Qian to lecture on the "Airs of the States."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived, he ordered Qian to lecture on the "Airs of the States" from the Book of Songs.

sentences.zh: 原講《堯典》，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Yuan lectured on the "Canon of Yao"; both pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan lectured on the "Canon of Yao"; both lectures pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 問何官，並以中允兼侍講對。

translations.literal: Asked what offices they held, both answered that they were Right and Left Secretaries concurrently serving as Readers-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When asked what offices they held, both replied that they were Right and Left Secretaries concurrently serving as Readers-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「品同耳，何相兼為？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: Their ranks are the same — why hold both offices?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Their ranks are the same — why hold both offices?

sentences.zh: 進二人侍講學士，兼中允。

translations.literal: Both were promoted to Reader-in-Waiting Academicians, concurrently serving as Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Both were promoted to Reader-in-Waiting Academicians, concurrently serving as Secretaries.

sentences.zh: 尋進左春坊大學士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Left Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Left Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 天順初，改通政司右參議，兼侍講。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was transferred to Right Assistant Commissioner of the Transmission Office, concurrently serving as Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianshun reign he was transferred to Right Assistant Commissioner of the Transmission Office, concurrently serving as Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 徐有貞、李賢下獄之明日，命入內閣預機務。

translations.literal: The day after Xu Youzhen and Li Xian were imprisoned, he was ordered to enter the Grand Secretariat and share in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Xu Youzhen and Li Xian were imprisoned, he was ordered into the Grand Secretariat to share in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 石享、曹吉祥用事，貴倨，獨敬原。

translations.literal: Shi Heng and Cao Jixiang held power, proud and arrogant; only Yuan was treated with respect.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng and Cao Jixiang held power, proud and overbearing; only Yuan was treated with respect.

sentences.zh: 原朝會衣青袍，亨笑曰：「行為先生易之。」

translations.literal: At court assemblies Yuan wore a green robe; Heng laughed and said: Before long we shall change that for you, sir.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies Yuan wore a green robe; Heng laughed and said: "Before long we shall change that for you, sir.

sentences.zh: 原不答。

translations.literal: Yuan did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan did not reply.

sentences.zh: 尋與嶽正列亨、吉祥罪狀，疏留中。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he and Yue Zheng listed the crimes of Heng and Jixiang; the memorial was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he and Yue Zheng listed the crimes of Heng and Jixiang in a memorial that was kept at court.

sentences.zh: 二人怒，摘敕諭中語，謂閣臣謗訕。

translations.literal: The two men were angry; they picked out phrases from an edict and said the Grand Secretariat ministers had slandered them.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were furious; they picked out phrases from an edict and accused the Grand Secretariat ministers of slander.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，坐便殿，召對，厲聲曰：「正大膽敢爾！

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered; seated in the side hall, he summoned them and said in a harsh voice: Zheng is bold to dare such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; seated in the side hall, he summoned them and said in a harsh voice: "Zheng is bold to dare such a thing!

sentences.zh: 原素恭謹，阿正何也？」

translations.literal: Yuan has always been respectful and cautious — why do you side with Zheng?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan has always been respectful and cautious — why do you side with Zheng?

sentences.zh: 正罷去，原得留。

translations.literal: Zheng was dismissed; Yuan was allowed to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was dismissed; Yuan was allowed to remain.

sentences.zh: 李賢既復官入閣柄政，原佐之。

translations.literal: After Li Xian was restored to office and entered the Grand Secretariat to wield power, Yuan assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xian was restored to office and entered the Grand Secretariat to wield power, Yuan assisted him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，彭時亦入，三人相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Before long Peng Shi also entered; the three men got on very well together.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Peng Shi also joined them; the three men worked together in great harmony.

sentences.zh: 賢通達，遇事立斷。

translations.literal: Xian was broad-minded and decided affairs on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was broad-minded and decisive in handling affairs.

sentences.zh: 原濟以持重，庶政稱理。

translations.literal: Yuan supplemented him with steadiness, and general administration was well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan complemented him with steadiness, and general administration was well ordered.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，進翰林院學士。

translations.literal: That winter he was promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 六年，遭母喪，水漿不入口三日。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he suffered his mother's death and took no food or drink for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he suffered his mother's death and took no food or drink for three days.

sentences.zh: 詔葬畢即起視事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to resume office as soon as the burial was complete.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to resume office as soon as the burial was complete.

sentences.zh: 原乞終制。

translations.literal: Yuan requested to complete the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan asked to complete the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: This was not granted.

sentences.zh: 乃之景州，啟父兄殯歸葬，舟中寢苫哀毀。

translations.literal: He then went to Jingzhou, opened the temporary coffins of his father and brother and returned them for burial; aboard the boat he slept on straw and mourned in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Jingzhou, opened the temporary coffins of his father and brother and returned them home for burial; aboard the boat he slept on straw mats and mourned in grief.

sentences.zh: 體素豐，至是羸瘠。

translations.literal: His body had always been robust; by now he was emaciated.
translations.idiomatic: He had always been robust of build; by now he was emaciated.

sentences.zh: 抵家甫襄事而卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: On reaching home he had just completed the funeral rites when he died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching home he had just completed the funeral rites when he died, at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部左侍郎，謚文懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Vice Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Left Vice Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 原內剛外和，與物無競。

translations.literal: Yuan was firm within and gentle without, contending with no one.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was firm within and gentle without, and contended with no one.

sentences.zh: 性儉約，身無紈綺。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal; he wore no silk finery.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was frugal and wore no silk finery.

sentences.zh: 歸裝惟賜衣數襲，分祿恤宗姻。

translations.literal: His returning baggage held only a few suits of granted clothing; he divided his salary to support kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: His returning baggage held only a few suits of granted clothing; he divided his salary to support kinsmen and in-laws.

sentences.zh: 子常，字秉之。

translations.literal: Zichang, style name Bingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zichang, styled Bingzhi.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補國子生，供事翰林，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he entered the Imperial Academy, served in the Hanlin, and was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he entered the Imperial Academy, served in the Hanlin Academy, and was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 疏乞應試，所司執故事不許。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting permission to sit for the examinations; the responsible office held to precedent and refused.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting permission to sit for the examinations; the responsible office held to precedent and refused.

sentences.zh: 憲宗特許之，遂舉順天鄉試。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong specially permitted it, and he then passed the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong specially permitted it, and he then passed the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 舍人得赴試自常始。

translations.literal: The permission for drafters to sit for examinations began with Zichang.
translations.idiomatic: The permission for drafters to sit for examinations began with Zichang.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部郎中，好學能文，諳掌故。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites; he loved learning, was skilled in writing, and knew institutional precedents well.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Director in the Ministry of Rites; he loved learning, wrote well, and knew institutional precedents thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 琉球請歲一入貢，回回貢使乞道廣東歸國，皆以非制格之。

translations.literal: Ryukyu requested annual tribute missions; Muslim tribute envoys asked to return home by way of Guangdong — both were rejected as contrary to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Ryukyu requested annual tribute missions, and Muslim tribute envoys asked to return home by way of Guangdong, he rejected both as contrary to regulations.

sentences.zh: 以薦進南京太仆寺少卿。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was promoted to Vice Director of the Nanjing Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was promoted to Vice Director of the Nanjing Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 故事，太仆馬數，不令他官知。

translations.literal: By precedent, the number of horses in the Imperial Stud was not to be known by other offices.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the number of horses in the Imperial Stud was not to be known by other offices.

sentences.zh: 以是文籍磨滅，登耗無稽。

translations.literal: Because of this the records were worn away and additions and losses could not be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the records had worn away and additions and losses could not be verified.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「他官不與聞，是也；

translations.literal: Zichang said: That other offices should not be informed is correct;
translations.idiomatic: Zichang said: "That other offices should not be informed is correct;

sentences.zh: 當職者，可貿貿耶？」

translations.literal: but can those who hold the office be so heedless?
translations.idiomatic: but can those who hold the office be so heedless?

sentences.zh: 議請三年一校勘，著為例。

translations.literal: He proposed a triennial audit and had it established as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a triennial audit and had it established as precedent.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京太常卿，輯《典故因革》若干卷。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of Ceremonies at Nanjing and compiled several volumes of Changes in Institutional Precedents.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of Ceremonies at Nanjing and compiled several volumes of Changes in Institutional Precedents.

sentences.zh: 正德初，致仕歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he retired and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengde reign he retired and returned home.

sentences.zh: 嶽正，字季方，漷縣人。

translations.literal: Yue Zheng, style name Jifang, was a native of Huo County.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Zheng, styled Jifang, was from Huo County.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年會試第一，賜進士及第，授編修，進左贊善。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he ranked first in the metropolitan examination, was granted jinshi status, appointed compiler, and promoted to Left Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong (1448), he ranked first in the metropolitan examination, passed the palace examination as a jinshi, was appointed a compiler, and promoted to Left Tutor.

sentences.zh: 天順初，改修撰，教小內侍書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was transferred to Drafting Compiler and taught young inner eunuchs to write.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianshun reign he was transferred to Drafting Compiler and taught young inner eunuchs to write.

sentences.zh: 閣臣徐有貞、李賢下獄，帝既用呂原預政，頃之，薛瑄又致仕，帝謀代者。

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat ministers Xu Youzhen and Li Xian were imprisoned; the emperor had already employed Lu Yuan in state affairs, and soon afterward Xue Xuan retired — the emperor sought a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: After Grand Secretariat ministers Xu Youzhen and Li Xian were imprisoned, the emperor had already brought Lu Yuan into state affairs; soon afterward Xue Xuan retired, and the emperor sought a replacement.

sentences.zh: 王翺以正薦，遂召見文華殿。

translations.literal: Wang Ao recommended Zheng, and he was summoned to audience in the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao recommended Zheng, and he was summoned to audience in the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 正長身美須髯，帝遙見，色喜。

translations.literal: Zheng was tall with a fine beard; seeing him from afar, the emperor's expression brightened.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was tall with a fine beard; seeing him from afar, the emperor's expression brightened with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 既登陛，連稱善。

translations.literal: Once he ascended the steps, the emperor repeatedly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he ascended the steps, the emperor repeatedly praised him.

sentences.zh: 問年幾何，家安在，何年進士，正具以對。

translations.literal: Asked his age, where his family dwelt, and in what year he became a jinshi, Zheng answered in full.
translations.idiomatic: Asked his age, where his family lived, and in what year he had become a jinshi, Zheng answered in full.

sentences.zh: 復大喜曰：「爾年正強仕，吾北人，又吾所取士，今用爾內閣，其盡力輔朕。」

translations.literal: Again greatly pleased, he said: "You are just in the prime of life; I am a northerner, and moreover you are one whom I selected as a scholar. Now I employ you in the Grand Secretariat — exert yourself fully to assist me.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly pleased again, he said, "You are just entering your prime; I am a northerner, and you are moreover a scholar I myself selected. Now that I am putting you in the Grand Secretariat, give me your full support.

sentences.zh: 正頓首受命。

translations.literal: Zheng kowtowed and accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng kowtowed and accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 趨出，石亨、張軏遇之左順門，愕然曰：「何自至此？」

translations.literal: He hurried out; Shi Heng and Zhang Yu encountered him at the Left Gate of Compliance and said in astonishment: "How did you come to be here?
translations.idiomatic: He hurried out, and Shi Heng and Zhang Yu ran into him at the Left Gate of Compliance. Astonished, they asked, "What brings you here?

sentences.zh: 比入，帝曰：「朕今日自擇一閣臣。」

translations.literal: When they entered, the emperor said: "Today I personally chose a Grand Secretariat minister.
translations.idiomatic: When they went in, the emperor said, "Today I chose a Grand Secretariat minister myself."

sentences.zh: 問為誰，帝曰：「嶽正。」

translations.literal: Asked who it was, the emperor said: "Yue Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Asked who it was, the emperor said, "Yue Zheng."

sentences.zh: 兩人陽賀。

translations.literal: The two men offered feigned congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The two men offered hollow congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「但官小耳，當與吏部左侍郎兼學士。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "His rank is merely low; he should be given Left Vice Minister of Personnel concurrently as a Bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "His rank is only low; he should be made Left Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent status as a Hanlin Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 兩人曰：「陛下既得人，俟稱職，加秩未晚。」

translations.literal: The two said: "Your Majesty has already obtained the right man; wait until he proves himself in office — it is not too late to raise his rank.
translations.idiomatic: The two said, "Your Majesty has already found the right man. Wait until he proves himself in office; there will be time enough to raise his rank."

sentences.zh: 帝默然，遂命以原官入閣。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent and ordered him to enter the Grand Secretariat at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing and ordered Zheng to enter the Grand Secretariat at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 正素豪邁，負氣敢言。

translations.literal: Zheng had always been bold and uninhibited, proud-spirited and daring to speak out.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had always been bold and outspoken, proud in spirit and unafraid to speak his mind.

sentences.zh: 及為帝所拔擢，益感激思自效。

translations.literal: Once elevated by the emperor, he was all the more filled with gratitude and determined to repay the favor.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had elevated him, he was all the more grateful and eager to prove his worth.

sentences.zh: 掌欽天監侍郎湯序者，亨黨也，嘗奏災異，請盡去奸臣。

translations.literal: Tang Xu, the Vice Director in charge of the Directorate of Astronomy, was a member of Heng's faction; he had once memorialized about portents and calamities, requesting that treacherous ministers be entirely removed.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xu, the Vice Director in charge of the Directorate of Astronomy, was one of Heng's allies. He had once memorialized about portents and calamities, asking that all treacherous ministers be removed.

sentences.zh: 帝問正，正言：「奸臣無指名。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Zheng; Zheng said: "The treacherous ministers are not named.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Zheng, who replied, "No treacherous ministers are named.

sentences.zh: 即求之，人人自危。

translations.literal: If one seeks them out, everyone will feel insecure.
translations.idiomatic: If you pursue the charge, everyone will feel threatened.

sentences.zh: 且序術淺，何足信也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Xu's skills are shallow — how can he be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Xu's learning is shallow — why should he be believed?

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 有僧為妖言，錦衣校邏得之，坐以謀反。

translations.literal: A monk spread heterodox talk; a brocade-clad guard named Bian Luo caught him and had him convicted of treason.
translations.idiomatic: A monk spread seditious talk; a brocade-clad guard named Bian Luo caught him and had him convicted of treason.

sentences.zh: 中官牛玉請官邏者，正言：「事縱得實，不過坐妖言律，邏者給賞而已，不宜與官。」

translations.literal: The inner eunuch Niu Yu requested that the informer be given an official post. Zheng said: "Even if the matter were proved true, at most it falls under the statute on heterodox talk — the informer should receive a reward, that is all; he should not be given an official post.
translations.idiomatic: The inner eunuch Niu Yu asked that the informer be given an official post. Zheng said, "Even if the case were proved, at most it would fall under the statute on seditious talk; the informer should receive a reward, nothing more. He should not be given office.

sentences.zh: 僧黨數十人皆得免。

translations.literal: Several dozen members of the monk's faction were all spared.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen people associated with the monk were all spared.

sentences.zh: 或為匿名書列曹吉祥罪狀，吉祥怒，請出榜購之。

translations.literal: Someone wrote an anonymous letter listing Cao Jixiang's crimes; Jixiang was enraged and requested that a placard be posted offering a reward for the informer.
translations.idiomatic: Someone wrote an anonymous letter listing Cao Jixiang's crimes. Jixiang was furious and asked that a public notice be posted offering a reward for the writer.

sentences.zh: 帝使正撰榜格，正與呂原入見曰：「為政有體，盜賊責兵部，奸宄責法司，豈有天子出榜購募者？

translations.literal: The emperor had Zheng draft the placard notice. Zheng and Lu Yuan entered audience and said: "Governance has its proper form: bandits are the responsibility of the Ministry of War, and evildoers the responsibility of the judicial offices — how can there be a Son of Heaven posting placards to offer rewards?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zheng draft the notice. Zheng and Lu Yuan came before him and said, "Government has its proper form: bandits are the Ministry of War's responsibility, and criminals the judiciary's. How can the Son of Heaven himself post notices offering rewards?

sentences.zh: 且事緩之則自露，急之則愈匿，此人情也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, if matters are handled slowly they reveal themselves; if pressed they are hidden all the more — such is human nature.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if a matter is handled slowly it will come to light on its own; if pressed, it will only be hidden all the more. That is human nature.

sentences.zh: 帝是其言，不問。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 亨從子彪鎮大同，獻捷，下內閣問狀。

translations.literal: Heng's nephew Biao, garrisoning Datong, reported a victory; the report was sent down to the Grand Secretariat to verify the details.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's nephew Biao, commanding at Datong, reported a victory, and the report was sent to the Grand Secretariat to verify the details.

sentences.zh: 使者言捕斬無算，不能悉致，皆梟置林木間。

translations.literal: The envoy said those captured and beheaded were beyond counting and could not all be brought in — all were displayed on poles among the trees.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said the number captured and beheaded was beyond counting and could not all be brought in; the heads had all been displayed on poles among the trees.

sentences.zh: 正按地圖指詰之，曰：「某地至某地，皆沙漠，汝梟置何所？」

translations.literal: Zheng traced the map and interrogated him, saying: "From such-and-such place to such-and-such place — all is desert; where did you display them on poles?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng studied the map and pressed him, saying, "From here to here it is all desert. Where did you display them on poles?

sentences.zh: 其人語塞。

translations.literal: The man was left speechless.
translations.idiomatic: The man had no answer.

sentences.zh: 時亨、吉祥恣甚，帝頗厭之。

translations.literal: At this time Heng and Jixiang were extremely overbearing, and the emperor had grown quite weary of them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Heng and Jixiang had become extremely overbearing, and the emperor had grown weary of them.

sentences.zh: 正從容言：「二人權太重，臣請以計間之。」

translations.literal: Zheng said calmly: "The two men's power is too great; your subject asks to use a stratagem to set them against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said calmly, "Those two have too much power. Your subject asks leave to use a stratagem to set them against each other.

sentences.zh: 帝許焉。

translations.literal: The emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 正出見吉祥曰：「忠國公常令杜清來此何為者？」

translations.literal: Zheng went out and saw Jixiang, saying: "Why is it that the Duke of Zhongguo often sends Du Qing here?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng went out and saw Jixiang. "Why does the Duke of Zhongguo keep sending Du Qing here?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 吉祥曰：「辱石公愛，致誠款耳。」

translations.literal: Jixiang said: "Out of Lord Shi's gracious favor — merely to offer sincere goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang said, "Out of Lord Shi's kindness — just to show sincere regard."

sentences.zh: 正曰：「不然，彼使伺公所為耳。」

translations.literal: Zheng said: "Not so — he sends him to spy on your doings.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "Not at all. He sends him to watch what you do."

sentences.zh: 因勸吉祥辭兵柄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he urged Jixiang to relinquish military power.
translations.idiomatic: Then he urged Jixiang to give up his military authority.

sentences.zh: 復詣亨，諭令自戢。

translations.literal: He then went to Heng and admonished him to restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Heng and told him to restrain himself.

sentences.zh: 亨、吉祥揣知正意，怒。

translations.literal: Heng and Jixiang guessed Zheng's intent and were enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and Jixiang saw through Zheng's plan and were furious.

sentences.zh: 吉祥見帝，免冠，泣請死。

translations.literal: Jixiang saw the emperor, removed his cap, and weeping begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang went to the emperor, removed his cap, and weeping asked to die.

sentences.zh: 帝內愧，慰諭之，召正責漏言。

translations.literal: The emperor felt inward shame, comforted and reassured him, and summoned Zheng to blame him for leaking the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor felt ashamed, comforted Jixiang, and summoned Zheng to rebuke him for letting the plan slip.

sentences.zh: 會承天門災，正極言亨將為不軌，且言：「陳汝言，小人。

translations.literal: When the Chengtian Gate burned, Zheng spoke forcefully that Heng was about to act treasonously, and also said: "Chen Ruyan is a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chengtian Gate burned, Zheng spoke bluntly that Heng was about to rebel. He also said, "Chen Ruyan is a petty man.

sentences.zh: 今既為尚書，可用盧彬為侍郎。

translations.literal: Now that he is Minister, Lu Bin can be used as Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is a minister, Lu Bin should be made vice minister.

sentences.zh: 二人者俱譎悍，若同事必相齮龁，乘其隙可並去之。」

translations.literal: Both men are crafty and fierce; if they work together they are sure to bite at each other — seize the opening and both can be removed together.
translations.idiomatic: Both are cunning and fierce. If they serve together they will surely tear at each other. Your Majesty can seize the opening and remove them both.

sentences.zh: 徐有貞再下獄，復云：「用有貞則天變可弭。」

translations.literal: Xu Youzhen was again imprisoned; Zheng also said: "If Youzhen is employed, the heavenly portent can be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Youzhen had again been imprisoned. Zheng also said, "If Youzhen is restored to office, the heavenly portent can be stilled."

sentences.zh: 帝皆不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept any of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected all of it.

sentences.zh: 及敕諭廷臣，命正視草。

translations.literal: When an edict was to instruct the court officials, the emperor ordered Zheng to draft it.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict was to be issued instructing the court, the emperor ordered Zheng to draft it.

sentences.zh: 正草敕曰：「乃者承天門災，朕心震驚，罔知所措。

translations.literal: Zheng drafted the edict: "Recently the Chengtian Gate suffered disaster; my heart was shaken with alarm, and I know not what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng drafted the edict: "Recently the Chengtian Gate was destroyed by fire. My heart was shaken with alarm, and I do not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 意敬天事神，有未盡歟？

translations.literal: Might reverence for Heaven and service to the spirits have been incomplete?
translations.idiomatic: Have I failed in reverence for Heaven and service to the spirits?

sentences.zh: 祖宗成憲有不遵歟？

translations.literal: Might the established statutes of the ancestral founders have gone unobserved?
translations.idiomatic: Have I failed to follow the established statutes of the ancestral founders?

sentences.zh: 善惡不分，用舍乖歟？

translations.literal: Might good and evil have gone undistinguished, and appointments and dismissals gone awry?
translations.idiomatic: Have good and evil gone undistinguished, and appointments and dismissals gone wrong?

sentences.zh: 曲直不辨，刑獄冤歟？

translations.literal: Might right and wrong have gone unjudged, and punishments and imprisonments been unjust?
translations.idiomatic: Have right and wrong gone unjudged, and punishments and imprisonments been unjust?

sentences.zh: 征調多方，軍旅勞歟？

translations.literal: Might levies and requisitions have been imposed from many quarters, and the armies worn with toil?
translations.idiomatic: Have levies and requisitions been imposed from too many quarters, wearing the armies with toil?

sentences.zh: 賞賚無度，府庫虛歟？

translations.literal: Might rewards and gifts have been dispensed without measure, and the treasuries emptied?
translations.idiomatic: Have rewards and gifts been dispensed without limit, emptying the treasuries?

sentences.zh: 請謁不息，官爵濫歟？

translations.literal: Might private petitions have gone unceasing, and offices and ranks been wantonly bestowed?
translations.idiomatic: Have private petitions never ceased, and offices and ranks been handed out recklessly?

sentences.zh: 賄賂公行，政事廢歟？

translations.literal: Might bribes have been openly traded, and government affairs neglected?
translations.idiomatic: Have bribes been traded openly, and government affairs neglected?

sentences.zh: 朋奸欺罔，附權勢歟？

translations.literal: Might corrupt factions have deceived and misled, clinging to power and influence?
translations.idiomatic: Have corrupt factions deceived and misled, clinging to power and influence?

sentences.zh: 群吏弄法，擅威福歟？

translations.literal: Might a host of officials have manipulated the law and arrogated authority and favor to themselves?
translations.idiomatic: Have officials manipulated the law and arrogated authority and favor to themselves?

sentences.zh: 征斂徭役太重，而閭閻靡寧歟？

translations.literal: Might exactions and corvée labor have been too heavy, so that households have known no peace?
translations.idiomatic: Have exactions and corvée labor been too heavy, leaving households without peace?

sentences.zh: 讒諂奔競之徒幸進，而忠言正士不用歟？

translations.literal: Might slanderers and flatterers scrambling for advancement have gained fortune, while loyal words and upright men have gone unused?
translations.idiomatic: Have slanderers and flatterers scrambling for advancement prospered, while loyal counsel and upright men have gone unused?

sentences.zh: 抑有司阘茸酷暴，貪冒無厭，而致軍民不得其所歟？

translations.literal: Or might subordinate officials have been incompetent, cruel, and violent, greedy and insatiable, so that soldiers and civilians have lost their proper place?
translations.idiomatic: Or have subordinate officials been incompetent, cruel, and violent, greedy without limit, so that soldiers and civilians have been left without their proper place?

sentences.zh: 此皆傷和致災之由，而朕有所未明也。

translations.literal: These are all causes that harm harmony and bring disaster — yet there are things of which I am not clear.
translations.idiomatic: These are all causes that disturb harmony and bring disaster — yet there are things here I do not understand.

sentences.zh: 今朕省愆思咎，怵惕是存。

translations.literal: Now I examine my faults and reflect on my transgressions, keeping fear and caution ever present.
translations.idiomatic: Now I examine my faults and reflect on my errors, keeping fear and caution ever in mind.

sentences.zh: 爾群臣休戚惟均，其洗心改過，無蹈前非，當行者直言無隱。」

translations.literal: You ministers share my weal and woe alike; cleanse your hearts, reform your errors, do not repeat past failings, and where action is due speak frankly without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: You ministers share my weal and woe alike. Cleanse your hearts, reform your ways, do not repeat past failings, and where action is needed speak frankly without concealment.

sentences.zh: 敕下，舉朝傳誦。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, the entire court passed it around and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, the whole court passed it around and read it aloud.

sentences.zh: 而亨、吉祥構蜚語，謂正賣直謗訕。

translations.literal: But Heng and Jixiang fabricated slander, saying Zheng was showing off his integrity and making derisive remarks.
translations.idiomatic: But Heng and Jixiang spread malicious rumors, saying Zheng was parading his integrity and making slanderous remarks.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命仍授內侍書。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered him returned to teaching the inner eunuchs to write.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and ordered him back to teaching the young inner eunuchs to write.

sentences.zh: 明日，謫欽州同知。

translations.literal: The next day he was demoted to Subprefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was demoted to subprefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 道漷，以母老留旬日。

translations.literal: Passing through Huo on the way, he stayed ten days because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: On the road at Huo, he stayed ten days because his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 陳汝言令巡校言狀，且言正嘗奪公主田。

translations.literal: Chen Ruyan had roaming guards report the situation, and also said Zheng had once seized a princess's land.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ruyan had roaming guards report what had happened, and also claimed that Zheng had once seized a princess's land.

sentences.zh: 遂逮系詔獄，杖百，戍肅州。

translations.literal: He was thereupon arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison, beaten one hundred strokes, and exiled to garrison duty at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then arrested and held in the imperial prison, beaten one hundred strokes, and exiled to garrison duty at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 行至涿，夜宿傳舍。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhuo, he lodged for the night at a relay station.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Zhuo, he spent the night at a relay station.

sentences.zh: 手拲急，氣奔且死。

translations.literal: His hand shackles were tight; his breath raced and he was near death.
translations.idiomatic: His hand shackles were too tight; he was gasping and near death.

sentences.zh: 涿人楊四醉卒酒，脫正拲，刳其中，且厚賂卒，乃得至戍所。

translations.literal: A Zhuo man named Yang Si, drunk, removed Zheng's shackles, hollowed out their insides, and also bribed the escort guards heavily — only then did he reach his garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhuo man named Yang Si, drunk on wine, removed Zheng's shackles, carved out their insides to loosen them, and bribed the escort guards heavily — only then did Zheng reach his place of exile.

sentences.zh: 亨、吉祥既誅，帝謂李賢曰：「嶽正固嘗言之。」

translations.literal: After Heng and Jixiang were executed, the emperor said to Li Xian: "Yue Zheng did indeed say as much before.
translations.idiomatic: After Heng and Jixiang were executed, the emperor said to Li Xian, "Yue Zheng had indeed said as much before.

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「正有老母，得放歸田裏，幸甚。」

translations.literal: Li Xian said: "Zheng has an aged mother; if he could be released to return to his fields, it would be a great mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian said, "Zheng has an aged mother. If he could be released to return home to his fields, it would be a great mercy."

sentences.zh: 乃釋為民。

translations.literal: Zheng was thereupon released and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was then released and restored to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，御史呂洪等請復正與楊瑄官，詔正以原官直經筵，纂修《英宗實錄》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, Censor Lu Hong and others requested restoration of office for Zheng and Yang Xuan; an edict ordered Zheng to his original post to attend the imperial lectures and compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, Censor Lu Hong and others asked that Zheng and Yang Xuan be restored to office. An edict ordered Zheng back to his original post to attend the imperial lectures and compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 初，正得罪，都督僉事季鐸乞得其宅，至是敕還正。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zheng had been condemned, Regional Commander Ji Duo had requested his residence; at this time an edict returned it to Zheng.
