translations.idiomatic: When Zheng had first been condemned, Regional Commander Ji Duo had asked for his house; now an edict returned it to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 正還朝，自謂當大用，而賢欲用為南京祭酒，正不悅。

translations.literal: Zheng returned to court, believing he would be greatly employed; but Xian wished to appoint him Chancellor of the Nanjing Imperial Academy, and Zheng was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng returned to court expecting a major appointment, but Xian wanted to make him Chancellor of the Nanjing Imperial Academy, and Zheng was displeased.

sentences.zh: 忌者偽為正劾賢疏草，賢嗛之。

translations.literal: Envious men forged a draft memorial by Zheng impeaching Xian, and Xian resented him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Envious men forged a draft memorial in Zheng's name impeaching Xian, and Xian resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 成化元年四月，廷推兵部侍郎清理貼黃，以正與給事中張寧名並上。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Chenghua, the court jointly recommended candidates for Vice Minister of War to clear pending memorial endorsements; Zheng's name and that of Supervising Secretary Zhang Ning were both submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Chenghua, the court jointly recommended candidates for Vice Minister of War to clear pending memorial endorsements. Both Zheng's name and that of Supervising Secretary Zhang Ning were put forward.

sentences.zh: 詔以為私，出正為興化知府，而寧亦補外。

translations.literal: An edict deemed it favoritism; Zheng was sent out as Prefect of Xinghua, and Ning also was assigned to an outer post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ruled the recommendation improper. Zheng was sent out as prefect of Xinghua, and Ning was also assigned to an outer post.

sentences.zh: 正至官，築堤溉田數千頃，節縮浮費，經理預備倉，欲有所興革。

translations.literal: When Zheng reached his post, he built dikes to irrigate several thousand qing of fields, cut unnecessary expenses, managed the reserve granaries, and wished to institute reforms.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, Zheng built dikes to irrigate several thousand qing of fields, cut unnecessary expenses, reorganized the reserve granaries, and sought to institute reforms.

sentences.zh: 鄉士大夫不利其所為，騰謗言。

translations.literal: Local gentry and officials opposed to his initiatives spread malicious rumors.
translations.idiomatic: Local gentry and officials who disliked his work spread malicious rumors.

sentences.zh: 正亦厭吏職，五年入覲，遂致仕。

translations.literal: Zheng also wearied of administrative office; after five years he came to court for audience and then retired.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng also grew weary of office. After five years he came to court for audience and then retired.

sentences.zh: 又五年卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: Five years later he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he died, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 無子，大學士李東陽、御史李經，其婿也。

translations.literal: He had no sons; Grand Secretary Li Dongyang and Censor Li Jing were his sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons. Grand Secretary Li Dongyang and Censor Li Jing were his sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 正博學能文章，高自期許，氣屹屹不能下人。

translations.literal: Zheng was broadly learned and skilled in composition, held himself to high expectations, and carried himself with such unyielding spirit that he would not defer to others.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was broadly learned and a strong writer. He set his sights high and carried himself with such unyielding pride that he would not defer to others.

sentences.zh: 在內閣才二十八日，勇事敢言，便殿論奏，至唾濺帝衣。

translations.literal: In the Grand Secretariat only twenty-eight days, he was bold in action and daring in speech; debating in the informal hall, he even splashed saliva on the emperor's robes.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Grand Secretariat for only twenty-eight days, yet was bold in action and fearless in speech. Debating in the informal hall, he even splashed saliva on the emperor's robes.

sentences.zh: 有規以信而後諫者，慨然曰：「上顧我厚，懼無以報稱，子乃以諫官處我耶？」

translations.literal: When someone cautioned him with "trust first, then remonstrate," he said with feeling: "The sovereign treats me generously, and I fear I cannot adequately repay his favor — yet you would treat me as a remonstrating official?
translations.idiomatic: When someone cautioned him to "establish trust first, then remonstrate," he said with feeling, "The sovereign treats me generously, and I fear I cannot repay his kindness — yet you would treat me like a remonstrating official?

sentences.zh: 英宗亦悉其忠，其在戍所，嘗念之曰：「嶽正倒好，只是大膽。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong also knew his loyalty fully; while Zheng was at his garrison post, he once recalled him, saying: "Yue Zheng is really quite good — only too bold.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong also knew his loyalty. While Zheng was in exile, he once recalled him, saying, "Yue Zheng is really quite good — only too bold."

sentences.zh: 正聞自為像贊，述帝前語，末言：「臣嘗聞古人之言，蓋將之死而靡憾也。」

translations.literal: Hearing this, Zheng wrote an inscription for his own portrait, recounting the emperor's earlier words, and at the end said: "Your subject once heard the words of the ancients — that one may approach death without regret.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard this, Zheng wrote an inscription for his own portrait, quoting the emperor's words, and at the end added, "Your subject once heard the ancients say that one may approach death without regret."

sentences.zh: 其自信不回如此。

translations.literal: Such was his unwavering self-confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his unshakable self-confidence.

sentences.zh: 然意廣才疏，欲以縱橫之術離散權黨，反為所噬，人皆迂而惜之。

translations.literal: Yet his aims were broad and his talents insufficient; wishing to use stratagems of alliance and division to scatter the power faction, he was instead devoured by them — everyone regarded him as impractical and lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his ambitions outran his abilities. Hoping to use divide-and-rule stratagems to break up the power faction, he was instead destroyed by them. People regarded him as impractical and regretted it.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，追贈太常寺卿，謚文肅。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he was posthumously ennobled as Director of Ceremonies and given the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing reign he was posthumously ennobled as Director of Ceremonies and given the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 彭時，字純道，安福人。

translations.literal: Peng Shi, styled Chundao, was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shi, styled Chundao, was from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he ranked first among jinshi, and was appointed Drafting Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong (1448) he ranked first among the jinshi and was appointed Drafting Compiler.

sentences.zh: 明年，郕王監國，令同商輅入閣預機務。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Prince of Cheng acted as regent, he was ordered together with Shang Lu to enter the Grand Secretariat and participate in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Prince of Cheng was regent, he was ordered together with Shang Lu to enter the Grand Secretariat and take part in confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 聞繼母憂，力辭，不允，乃拜命。

translations.literal: Hearing of his stepmother's death, he strenuously declined but was not permitted to do so, and accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned of his stepmother's death, he tried hard to decline, but was not allowed to do so and accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 釋褐逾年參大政，前此未有也。

translations.literal: To join major government within a year of first taking office had never happened before.
translations.idiomatic: To take part in major government within a year of first entering office was unprecedented.

sentences.zh: 尋進侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，以兵事稍息，得請終制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, as military affairs had eased somewhat, he obtained permission to complete mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai (1450), as military affairs had eased somewhat, he obtained permission to complete his mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 然由此忤旨。

translations.literal: Yet by this he went against the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in doing so he fell out of favor with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 服除，命供事翰林院，不復與閣事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was ordered to serve the Hanlin Academy and no longer take part in Grand Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he was assigned to the Hanlin Academy and was no longer involved in Grand Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 易儲，遷左春坊大學士。

translations.literal: At the change of heir, he was transferred to Left Chancellor of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was changed, he was transferred to Left Chancellor of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 《寰宇通志》成，遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm was completed, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm was completed, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 俱兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Both posts were held concurrently with Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He held both posts concurrently as Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 天順元年，徐有貞既得罪，嶽正、許彬相繼罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun, after Xu Youzhen had been condemned, Yue Zheng and Xu Bin were dismissed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianshun (1457), after Xu Youzhen had fallen from grace, Yue Zheng and Xu Bin were dismissed one after another.

sentences.zh: 帝坐文華殿召見時，曰：「汝非朕所擢狀元乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor, seated in the Wenhua Hall, summoned Shi for an audience and said: "Are you not the palace graduate whom I personally selected?
translations.idiomatic: Seated in the Wenhua Hall, the emperor summoned Shi and asked, "Are you not the top graduate I personally chose?

sentences.zh: 時頓首。

translations.literal: Shi kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi kowtowed in reply.

sentences.zh: 明日仍命入閣，兼翰林院學士。

translations.literal: The next day he was again ordered to enter the Grand Secretariat, concurrently as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor again ordered him into the Grand Secretariat, with concurrent appointment as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 閣臣自三楊後，進退禮甚輕。

translations.literal: Since the Three Yangs, the rites governing appointment and dismissal of Grand Secretariat ministers had been very casually observed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the era of the Three Yangs, little ceremony had attended the appointment and dismissal of Grand Secretariat ministers.

sentences.zh: 為帝所親擢者，唯時與正二人。

translations.literal: Of those personally promoted by the emperor, only Shi and Zheng were two.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shi and Zheng had been personally elevated by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 而帝方向用李賢，數召賢獨對。

translations.literal: But the emperor was inclined to employ Li Xian and repeatedly summoned Xian for private audience.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor was turning to Li Xian and repeatedly summoned him for private consultations.

sentences.zh: 賢雅重時，退必咨之。

translations.literal: Xian always held Shi in esteem; upon leaving audience he invariably consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian always respected Shi highly and unfailingly sought his counsel after leaving the emperor's presence.

sentences.zh: 時引義爭可否，或至失色。

translations.literal: Shi would cite principle to argue for or against, sometimes even changing countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Shi would appeal to principle in debating each point, at times to the point of losing composure.

sentences.zh: 賢初小忤，久亦服其諒直，曰：「彭公，真君子也。」

translations.literal: At first Xian was somewhat displeased, but in time he came to admire his integrity and candor, saying: "Lord Peng is a true gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was initially a little offended, but over time he came to admire Shi's honesty and forthrightness, saying, "Lord Peng is a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 慈壽皇太后上尊號，詔告天下。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager Cishou was granted an honorific title, an edict announced it to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Cishou was given an honorific title, an edict proclaimed it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 時欲推恩，賢謂一年不宜再赦。

translations.literal: Shi wished to extend grace; Xian said that within one year it was not proper to grant another amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Shi wished to extend imperial grace, but Xian argued that it was inadvisable to issue another general amnesty within the same year.

sentences.zh: 時曰：「非赦也，宜行優老典。

translations.literal: Shi said: "It is not an amnesty; the proper course is to enact the rites honoring the aged.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "This is not an amnesty — we should instead put into practice the rites honoring the elderly.

sentences.zh: 朝臣父母七十與誥敕，百姓八十給冠帶，是『老吾老以及人之老』也。」

translations.literal: Officials whose parents had reached seventy would receive edicts of commendation; commoners at eighty would be granted caps and sashes — this is to honor one's own elders and extend that honor to the elders of others.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials whose parents had reached seventy would receive letters of commendation, and commoners of eighty would be given ceremonial caps and sashes — embodying the principle of honoring one's own elders and extending that care to the elders of others.

sentences.zh: 賢稱善，即奏行之。

translations.literal: Xian praised the plan as good and immediately memorialized to put it into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Xian approved, and immediately submitted a memorial to enact the proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝愛時風度，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: The emperor admired Shi's bearing and entrusted him with selecting junior Hanlin scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired Shi's bearing and put him in charge of selecting junior Hanlin scholars.

sentences.zh: 命賢盡用北人，南人必若時者方可。

translations.literal: He ordered Xian to employ northerners entirely; southerners could be used only if they were like Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Xian to appoint northerners exclusively; southerners could be selected only if they were men of Shi's caliber.

sentences.zh: 賢以語時。

translations.literal: Xian told this to Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Xian related this to Shi.

sentences.zh: 俄中官牛玉宣旨，時謂玉曰：「南士出時上者不少，何可抑之？」

translations.literal: Before long the eunuch Niu Yu proclaimed the imperial decree; Shi said to Yu: "Among southern scholars there are many who surpass Shi — how can they be suppressed?
translations.idiomatic: Before long the eunuch Niu Yu announced the imperial instruction. Shi said to him, "There are many southern scholars who surpass even Shi — how can they be held back?

sentences.zh: 已，選十五人，南六人與焉。

translations.literal: When done, fifteen were selected, six southerners among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the end fifteen were selected, six of them southerners.

sentences.zh: 門達構賢，帝惑之，曰：「去賢，行專用時矣。」

translations.literal: Men Da framed Xian; the emperor was misled and said: "Remove Xian — then I will rely on Shi alone.
translations.idiomatic: Men Da slandered Xian, and the emperor was taken in, saying, "Remove Xian, and I will rely on Shi alone.

sentences.zh: 或傳其語，時矍然曰：「李公有經濟才，何可去？」

translations.literal: When someone relayed these words, Shi started and said: "Lord Li has talent for governing — how can he be removed?"
translations.idiomatic: When word of this reached him, Shi was startled and said, "Lord Li has real ability in statecraft — he cannot be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 因力直之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he strenuously defended him.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon vigorously defended Xian.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「賢去，時不得獨留。」

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "If Xian goes, Shi cannot remain alone.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If Xian goes, I cannot remain by myself.

sentences.zh: 語聞，帝意乃解。

translations.literal: When these words were reported, the emperor's mind was set at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, his suspicions were dispelled.

sentences.zh: 帝大漸，口占遺命，定後妃名分，勿以嬪禦殉葬，凡四事，付閣臣潤色。

translations.literal: As the emperor grew gravely ill, he orally dictated his final testament — fixing the titles of consorts and secondary wives, forbidding concubines to be buried alive in sacrifice, four matters in all — and entrusted them to Grand Secretariat ministers to polish in writing.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's condition worsened, he dictated his dying instructions — settling the titles of consorts, forbidding the burial of concubines in live sacrifice, four matters in all — and handed them to the Grand Secretariat ministers to draft in proper form.

sentences.zh: 時讀竟，涕下，悲愴不自勝。

translations.literal: When Shi had finished reading, tears fell; grief overcame him beyond his power to bear.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi had finished reading, he wept, overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 中官復命，帝亦為隕涕。

translations.literal: The eunuch reported back, and the emperor too shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch reported back, the emperor wept as well.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，議上兩宮尊號。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, deliberation began on granting honorific titles to the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, the court deliberated on honorific titles for the two empress dowagers.

sentences.zh: 中官夏時希周貴妃旨，言錢後久病，不當稱太后。

translations.literal: The eunuch Xia Shi, hoping to please Noble Consort Zhou, said Empress Qian had long been ill and ought not be called Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Xia Shi, acting on Noble Consort Zhou's wishes, argued that Empress Qian had long been ill and should not be granted the title Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 而貴妃，帝所生母，宜獨上尊號。

translations.literal: The Noble Consort, however — the emperor's birth mother — ought alone to receive an honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: The Noble Consort, the emperor's biological mother, should alone receive the honorific title.

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「遺詔已定，何事多言。」

translations.literal: Xian said: "The final testament is already settled — what need for further words?
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "The dying edict has already settled this — why raise it again?

sentences.zh: 時曰：「李公言是也。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Lord Li's words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "Lord Li is right.

sentences.zh: 朝廷所以服天下，在正綱常。

translations.literal: The reason the court commands the allegiance of the realm lies in upholding the proper order of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: The court earns the loyalty of the realm by upholding proper moral order.

sentences.zh: 若不爾，損聖德非小。」

translations.literal: If otherwise, the harm to imperial virtue would not be small."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the damage to the emperor's moral standing would be considerable."

sentences.zh: 頃之，中官復傳貴妃旨：「子為皇帝，母當為太后，豈有無子而稱太后者？

translations.literal: Before long the eunuch again conveyed the Noble Consort's wish: "When the son is emperor, the mother ought to be empress dowager — how can one without a son be called empress dowager?
translations.idiomatic: Before long the eunuch relayed the Noble Consort's message again: "The son is emperor, so his mother should be empress dowager — can a woman without a son bear that title?

sentences.zh: 宣德間有故事。」

translations.literal: In the Xuande era there was a precedent."
translations.idiomatic: There was a precedent from the Xuande reign."

sentences.zh: 賢色變，目時。

translations.literal: Xian's countenance changed; he signaled with his eyes to Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's expression changed, and he looked to Shi for a response.

sentences.zh: 時曰：「今日事與宣德間不同。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Today's matter differs from that of the Xuande era.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "Today's situation is not the same as in the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 胡後表讓位，退居別宮，故在正統初不加尊。

translations.literal: Empress Hu formally petitioned to yield her place and retired to a separate palace; hence at the beginning of Zhengtong no honorific title was granted her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hu had formally petitioned to yield her position and retired to a separate palace, which is why no honorific was granted her at the start of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 今名分固在，安得為比？」

translations.literal: Now the title is fixed in place — how can the two cases be compared?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qian's status is already established — the cases cannot be equated.

sentences.zh: 中官曰：「如是何不草讓表？」

translations.literal: The eunuch said: "If so, why not draft a petition of yielding?"
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch said, "In that case, why not draft a petition for her to yield her title?"

sentences.zh: 時曰：「先帝存日未嘗行，今誰敢草？

translations.literal: Shi said: "While the late emperor lived this was never done — who now dares draft it?
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "The late emperor never permitted this while he lived — who would dare draft such a document now?

sentences.zh: 若人臣阿意順從，是萬世罪人也。」

translations.literal: If as minister one flatters and complies, one becomes a criminal for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: If we ministers simply flatter and comply, we will be condemned through the ages."

sentences.zh: 中官厲聲怵以危語。

translations.literal: The eunuch raised his voice and threatened with words of danger.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch raised his voice and tried to intimidate them with threats.

sentences.zh: 時拱手向天曰：「太祖、太宗神靈在上，孰敢有二心！

translations.literal: Shi clasped his hands and faced heaven, saying: "The spirits of Taizu and Taizong watch from above — who would dare harbor divided loyalties!
translations.idiomatic: Shi clasped his hands toward heaven and declared, "The spirits of Taizu and Taizong are watching — who would dare be disloyal!

sentences.zh: 錢皇后無子，何所規利而為之爭？

translations.literal: Empress Qian has no son — what profit does she seek that she would fight for this?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qian has no son — what personal gain could she possibly seek in pressing this claim?

sentences.zh: 臣義不忍默者，欲全主上聖德耳。

translations.literal: The reason this subject cannot bear to remain silent is that he wishes to preserve the sage virtue of his lord.
translations.idiomatic: I speak out because, as a subject, I cannot in good conscience stay silent — I mean only to safeguard the emperor's moral reputation.

sentences.zh: 若推大孝之心，則兩宮並尊為宜。」

translations.literal: If one extends the mind of great filial piety, then honoring both palaces equally is proper.
translations.idiomatic: If we act from the deepest filial devotion, it is right that both empresses be honored equally.

sentences.zh: 賢亦極言之，議遂定。

translations.literal: Xian also argued to the utmost, and the deliberation was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xian also pressed the point forcefully, and the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 及將上寶冊，時曰：「兩宮同稱則無別，錢太后宜加兩字，以便稱謂。」

translations.literal: When the imperial patent was about to be presented, Shi said: "If both palaces bear the same title, there will be no distinction — Empress Dowager Qian should have two additional characters added to facilitate address.
translations.idiomatic: As the presentation of the imperial honors was about to proceed, Shi said, "If both bear the same title there will be no way to tell them apart — two additional characters should be added to Empress Dowager Qian's title for ease of address.

sentences.zh: 乃尊為慈懿皇太后，貴妃為皇太后。

translations.literal: Thereupon she was honored as Empress Dowager Ciyi, and the Noble Consort as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qian was honored as Empress Dowager Ciyi, and the Noble Consort as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 越數日，中官覃包至內閣曰：「上意固如是。

translations.literal: Several days later the eunuch Tan Bao came to the Grand Secretariat and said: "His Majesty's intent was indeed thus.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the eunuch Tan Bao came to the Grand Secretariat and said, "The emperor's intention was always as you argued.

sentences.zh: 但迫於太后，不敢自主，非二公力急，幾誤大事。」

translations.literal: But pressed by the Empress Dowager, he dared not decide for himself; were it not for the two lords' forceful urgency, a great matter would nearly have been botched.
translations.idiomatic: But constrained by the empress dowager, he dared not decide on his own — had the two of you not pressed so hard, a grave mistake would nearly have been made.

sentences.zh: 時閣臣陳文默無語，聞包言，甚愧。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Secretariat minister Chen Wen had been silent; hearing Bao's words, he was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat minister Chen Wen had said nothing throughout; when he heard Bao's words, he was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 禮成，進吏部右侍郎，兼學士，同知經筵。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Personnel, concurrently Academician, and Associate Director of the Imperial Lectures.
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremonies were completed, he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Personnel, with concurrent appointment as Academician and Associate Director of the Imperial Lectures.

sentences.zh: 成化改元，進兵部尚書，兼官如故。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title to Chenghua, he was promoted to Minister of War; his concurrent posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title was changed to Chenghua, he was promoted to Minister of War while keeping his concurrent appointments unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，乞歸省。

translations.literal: The next autumn he requested leave to return home and visit family.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he asked for leave to visit his family at home.

sentences.zh: 三年二月詔趣還朝，《英宗實錄》成，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year an edict hastened his return to court; when the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong were completed, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year an edict recalled him to court; when the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong were completed, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 兼文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: Concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 四年，慈懿太后崩，詔議山陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Empress Dowager Ciyi died; an edict ordered deliberation on her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Empress Dowager Ciyi died, and the court was ordered to deliberate on her burial arrangements.

sentences.zh: 時及商輅、劉定之言：「太后作配先帝，正位中宮，陛下尊為太后，詔示天下。

translations.literal: Shi together with Shang Lu and Liu Dingzhi said: "The Empress Dowager was consort to the late emperor and held the central position in the inner palace; Your Majesty honored her as empress dowager and proclaimed it to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, along with Shang Lu and Liu Dingzhi, said, "The empress dowager was the late emperor's rightful consort in the central palace; Your Majesty honored her as empress dowager and proclaimed it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 先帝全夫婦之倫，陛下盡母子之愛，於義俱得。

translations.literal: The late emperor fulfilled the ethics of husband and wife; Your Majesty has exhaustively shown the love of mother and son — in principle both are satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor fulfilled the bond between husband and wife, and Your Majesty has shown complete filial devotion — both obligations are properly met.

sentences.zh: 今梓宮當合葬裕陵，主當祔廟，此不易之禮。

translations.literal: Now the coffin ought to be interred jointly at Yuling, and her spirit tablet ought to be installed in the ancestral temple — this is unalterable rite.
translations.idiomatic: Her coffin should be interred alongside the late emperor at Yuling, and her spirit tablet placed in the ancestral temple — this is established ritual that should not be changed.

sentences.zh: 比聞欲別卜葬地，臣等實懷疑懼。

translations.literal: Recently we have heard of a wish to select a separate burial site; your subjects truly harbor doubt and fear.
translations.idiomatic: We have recently heard that a separate burial site may be chosen, and we are deeply troubled by the prospect.

sentences.zh: 竊謂皇上所以遲疑者，必以今皇太后萬壽後，當與先帝同尊，自嫌二後並配，非祖宗制。

translations.literal: We venture to say that the reason Your Majesty hesitates must be that after the present Empress Dowager's long life ends, she too should be honored equally with the late emperor, and you yourself feel that two empresses sharing the consort's place is not ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: We suspect Your Majesty hesitates because, after the present empress dowager's death, she too will deserve equal honor with the late emperor — and you may worry that having two empresses share the consort's place violates ancestral precedent.

sentences.zh: 考之於古，漢文帝尊所生母薄太后，而呂後仍祔長陵。

translations.literal: Examining antiquity, Emperor Wen of Han honored his birth mother Empress Dowager Bo, yet Empress Lü was still installed at Changling.
translations.idiomatic: History provides precedent: Emperor Wen of Han honored his birth mother Empress Dowager Bo, yet Empress Lü's spirit tablet remained at Changling.

sentences.zh: 宋仁宗追尊生母李宸妃，而劉後仍祔太廟。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong of Song posthumously honored his birth mother Consort Li, yet Empress Liu was still installed in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong of Song posthumously honored his birth mother Consort Li, yet Empress Liu's tablet remained in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 今若陵廟之制稍有未合，則有乖前美，貽譏來葉。」

translations.literal: Now if the institutions of tomb and temple even slightly fail to accord, it would depart from past excellence and invite ridicule from future generations.
translations.idiomatic: If the arrangements for tomb and temple deviate even slightly from proper form, we will fall short of past exemplars and invite censure from future ages.

sentences.zh: 於是諸大臣相繼言之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various senior ministers spoke in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers spoke up one after another in support.

sentences.zh: 帝猶重違太后意，時偕朝臣伏文華門泣請。

translations.literal: The emperor still greatly feared going against the Empress Dowager's wish; Shi together with court officials prostrated themselves at the Wenhua Gate, weeping as they petitioned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still dreaded defying the empress dowager's wishes, so Shi and other officials knelt and wept in petition at the Wenhua Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝與太后皆感動，始從時議。

translations.literal: Both emperor and empress dowager were moved, and only then did he follow Shi's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Both the emperor and the empress dowager were moved, and the emperor finally accepted Shi's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 彗見三臺，時等言：「外廷大政固所當先，宮中根本尤為至急。

translations.literal: A comet appeared in the Three Terraces; Shi and others said: "Although outer-court great affairs ought naturally to come first, the root of the inner palace is especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared in the Three Terraces asterism, Shi and others said, "Outer-court affairs must naturally come first, but the foundation of the inner palace is even more urgent.

sentences.zh: 諺雲『子出多母』。

translations.literal: A proverb says: 'Many mothers, yet still no son.'
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, 'Many mothers, yet still no son.'

sentences.zh: 今嬪嬙眾多，維熊無兆。

translations.literal: Now palace ladies and consorts are numerous, yet there is no auspicious sign of a bear.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace is filled with consorts, yet there is no sign of pregnancy.

sentences.zh: 必陛下愛有所專，而專寵者已過生育之期故也。

translations.literal: It must be that Your Majesty's love has a single object, and the specially favored one has already passed the age of childbearing.
translations.idiomatic: This must be because Your Majesty's affection is concentrated on one woman who is already past childbearing age.

sentences.zh: 望均恩愛，為宗社大計。」

translations.literal: We hope Your Majesty will distribute affection equally, for the great plan of altars of state and ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: We urge Your Majesty to share your affection more broadly, for the sake of the dynasty's future.

sentences.zh: 時帝專寵萬貴妃，妃年已近四十，時故云然。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor specially favored Consort Wan; the consort's age was already nearly forty — hence Shi spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was devoted exclusively to Consort Wan, who was already nearly forty — which is why Shi said what he did.

sentences.zh: 又言：「大臣黜陟，宜斷自宸衷，或集群臣僉議。

translations.literal: He also said: "Appointment and dismissal of great ministers ought to be decided from the imperial heart, or by assembling ministers for collective deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The promotion and dismissal of senior ministers should be decided by Your Majesty personally, or through collective deliberation among the ministers.

sentences.zh: 不可悉委臣下，使大權旁落。」

translations.literal: One must not entirely delegate to subjects below, causing great power to slip aside.
translations.idiomatic: Authority must not be entirely delegated to subordinates, lest supreme power pass into other hands.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不能從，而心嘉其忠。

translations.literal: The emperor though unable to follow, in his heart admired his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not follow this advice, but he admired Shi's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 都御史項忠討滿四不利。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xiang Zhong's campaign against Man Si went unfavorably.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Xiang Zhong's campaign against the rebel Man Si was going poorly.

sentences.zh: 朝議命撫寧侯朱永將京軍往赴。

translations.literal: Court deliberation ordered Marquis of Zoning Zhu Yong to lead capital troops to go assist.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided to send the Marquis of Zoning Zhu Yong at the head of capital troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 永故難其行，多所邀請。

translations.literal: Yong deliberately made difficulties about marching, making many demands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yong deliberately delayed his departure, making numerous demands.

sentences.zh: 時惡其張大，且度軍可無行，第令整裝待。

translations.literal: Shi detested his grandiose airs, and moreover judged that the army need not march — merely ordering preparations to await.
translations.idiomatic: Shi resented Zhu Yong's arrogance and judged that the troops need not be sent at all; he merely ordered them to stand ready.

sentences.zh: 會忠馳奏，已圍賊石城。

translations.literal: Just then Zhong sent a rapid memorial: he had already besieged the rebels at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Xiang Zhong sent an urgent report that he had already besieged the rebels at Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官懷恩、黃賜偕兵部尚書白圭、程信等至閣議。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched eunuchs Huai En and Huang Ci together with Ministers of War Bai Gui, Cheng Xin, and others to the Grand Secretariat for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuchs Huai En and Huang Ci, together with the Minister of War Bai Gui, Cheng Xin, and others, to the Grand Secretariat to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 時曰：「賊四出攻剽，鋒誠不可當。

translations.literal: Shi said: "The bandits raid in all directions; their edge truly cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "The rebels have been raiding in every direction — their momentum is truly formidable.

sentences.zh: 今入石城自保，我軍圍甚固，此困獸易擒耳。」

translations.literal: Now having entered Shicheng to protect themselves, our army's siege is very solid — these are cornered beasts, easy to capture.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have withdrawn into Shicheng for safety, and our encirclement is tight — cornered beasts like these are easily taken.

sentences.zh: 信曰：「安知忠不退師？」

translations.literal: Xin said: "How do we know Zhong will not withdraw his army?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xin said, "How can we be sure Xiang Zhong won't pull his forces back?"

sentences.zh: 時曰：「彼部分已定，何故自退？

translations.literal: Shi said: "Their dispositions are already fixed — for what reason would they withdraw on their own?
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "His deployments are already set — why would he withdraw on his own initiative?

sentences.zh: 且今出師，度何時到？」

translations.literal: Moreover, if troops march out now, estimate when they would arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: And if we dispatch troops now, when would they even arrive?"

sentences.zh: 信曰：「來春。」

translations.literal: Xin said: "Next spring."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xin said, "Not until next spring."

sentences.zh: 時曰：「如此，益緩不及事。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Thus, all the more leisurely — too late for the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "In that case we would only arrive too late to matter.

sentences.zh: 事成敗，冬月決矣。」

translations.literal: Success or failure in the affair will be decided in the winter months."
translations.idiomatic: The outcome will be decided this winter."

sentences.zh: 信忿，出危言曰：「忠若敗，必斬一二人，然後出師。」

translations.literal: Xin was angry and spoke alarming words, saying: "If Zhong should fail, one or two men must be beheaded, and only then may the army march out."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xin, furious, spoke bluntly: "If Xiang Zhong fails, someone will have to lose his head before we send troops."

sentences.zh: 眾危之，問時何見。

translations.literal: The assembly found this alarming and asked Shi what insight he had.
translations.idiomatic: The others were alarmed and asked Peng Shi what he saw in the situation.

sentences.zh: 曰：「觀忠疏曲折，知其能。

translations.literal: He said: "Observing the twists and turns in Zhong's memorial, I know his ability.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Reading the detail in Xiang Zhong's memorial, I can see he knows what he is doing.

sentences.zh: 若聞別遣禁軍，將退避不敢任，賊不可知矣。」

translations.literal: If he hears that capital troops are separately dispatched, the general will shrink back and not dare to accept responsibility — the bandits' outcome would be unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: If he learns that the capital is sending a separate force, he will pull back and refuse to commit himself — and the rebels' fate will become impossible to predict.

sentences.zh: 時惟商輅然其言。

translations.literal: Only Shang Lu agreed with Shi's words.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shang Lu agreed with Peng Shi.

sentences.zh: 至冬，賊果平，人乃大服。

translations.literal: By winter the bandits were indeed pacified, and people came greatly to admire him.
translations.idiomatic: By winter the rebels had indeed been suppressed, and people came to admire him greatly.

sentences.zh: 改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 五年得疾在告。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he fell ill and took leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he fell ill and went on sick leave.

sentences.zh: 逾三月，帝趣赴閣視事，免朝參。

translations.literal: After more than three months the emperor urged him to come to the Grand Secretariat and resume duties, exempting him from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After more than three months the emperor pressed him to return to the Grand Secretariat and resume work, exempting him from daily court attendance.

sentences.zh: 是冬，無雪。

translations.literal: That winter there was no snow.
translations.idiomatic: That winter brought no snow.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「光祿寺采辦，各城門抽分，掊克不堪。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The procurement of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, with levies at each city gate, extorts unbearably.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The Court of Imperial Entertainments' procurement agents, with their levies at every city gate, squeeze the people past endurance.

sentences.zh: 而獻珍珠寶石者，倍估增直，漁竭帑藏。

translations.literal: Those presenting pearls and precious stones have prices doubled and values inflated, fishing dry the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Those who offered pearls and gems had their prices doubled and inflated, draining the treasury dry.

sentences.zh: 乞革其弊，以惠小民。」

translations.literal: I beg to abolish these abuses, to benefit the common people.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these abuses be abolished for the benefit of the common people.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔褒納。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict praising and accepting it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with a gracious edict of praise and acceptance.

sentences.zh: 畿輔、山東、河南旱，請免夏稅鹽鈔，及太仆寺賠課馬。

translations.literal: In the capital region, Shandong, and Henan there was drought; he requested exemption from summer tax and salt certificates, and compensation horses demanded by the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck the capital region, Shandong, and Henan, he asked that summer taxes and salt certificates be remitted and that the Court of Imperial Stud's levies for compensation horses be waived.

sentences.zh: 京師米貴，請發倉儲五十萬石平糶。

translations.literal: Grain was expensive in the capital; he requested releasing five hundred thousand shi from storehouses for fair-price sale.
translations.idiomatic: With grain prices soaring in the capital, he asked that five hundred thousand shi be released from the granaries for relief sale at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were granted.
translations.idiomatic: All these requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 時以舊臣見倚重，遇事爭執無所避。

translations.literal: Shi, as an old minister upon whom the emperor relied, argued over affairs without holding back.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior minister in whom the emperor placed great trust, Shi argued his points without flinching.

sentences.zh: 而是時帝怠於政，大臣希得見。

translations.literal: Yet at this time the emperor was slack in government, and great ministers seldom gained audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor had grown negligent in government, and senior ministers rarely obtained an audience.

sentences.zh: 萬安同在閣，結中貴戚畹，上下壅隔，時頗懷憂。

translations.literal: Wan An was also in the Grand Secretariat, allied with influential eunuchs and imperial affines; communication between above and below was blocked, and Shi was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An served alongside him in the Grand Secretariat, cultivating ties with powerful eunuchs and imperial in-laws; with communication between throne and ministers choked off, Shi grew deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 七年，疾復作，乞致仕。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his illness recurred; he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year his illness returned, and he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留之，不得去。

translations.literal: The emperor consoled him and kept him; he could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him and kept him at his post; he was not permitted to leave.

sentences.zh: 冬，彗復見，時言政本七事：一，毋惑佛事，糜金錢；

translations.literal: In winter a comet appeared again; Shi spoke of seven fundamentals of governance: first, do not be deluded by Buddhist affairs, squandering gold and money;
translations.idiomatic: That winter a comet appeared again, and Shi set forth seven foundations of good government: first, do not be led astray by Buddhist rites that squander gold and silver;

sentences.zh: 二，傳旨專委司禮監，毋令他人，以防詐偽；

translations.literal: second, entrust the transmission of imperial orders exclusively to the Directorate of Ceremonial, not permitting others, to guard against fraud;
translations.idiomatic: second, confide the transmission of imperial orders exclusively to the Directorate of Ceremonial and to no one else, to guard against forgery;

sentences.zh: 三，延見大臣議政事；

translations.literal: third, receive great ministers in audience to discuss state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: third, summon senior ministers to audience to deliberate on state affairs;

sentences.zh: 四，近幸賜予太多，工匠冒官無紀，而重囚死徙者，法不蔽罪。

translations.literal: fourth, favorites receive too much in gifts; artisans falsely claim official positions without restraint; yet for serious criminals condemned to death or banishment, the law fails to cover their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, favorites receive excessive gifts; artisans falsely claim official rank without restraint; yet for serious offenders condemned to death or exile, the law fails to reach them;

sentences.zh: 宜戒淫刑僭賞；

translations.literal: one should guard against excessive punishments and improper rewards;
translations.idiomatic: the court should guard against excessive punishments and improper rewards;

sentences.zh: 五，虛懷受諫，勿惡切直；

translations.literal: fifth, receive admonition with an open mind, and do not hate blunt forthrightness;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, receive remonstrance with an open mind and do not resent blunt speech;

sentences.zh: 六，戒廷臣毋依違，凡政令失當，直言論奏；

translations.literal: sixth, warn court ministers not to waver; whenever policies are improper, speak forthrightly in memorials;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, warn court ministers against equivocation — whenever a policy is wrong, speak out plainly in memorials;

sentences.zh: 七，清理牧馬草地，減退勢要莊田。

translations.literal: seventh, clear up pasture lands for horse herding, and reduce the estate fields of the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: seventh, restore pasture lands used for horse herding and roll back the estate holdings of the powerful.

sentences.zh: 皆切中時弊。

translations.literal: All struck directly at the ills of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Every point went straight to the abuses of the day.

sentences.zh: 寧晉伯劉聚為從父太監永誠請封謚，且乞祠額，禮部執故事卻之。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Ningjin Liu Ju petitioned on behalf of his father's younger brother, the eunuch Yongcheng, for ennoblement and posthumous title, and also requested a shrine plaque; the Ministry of Rites insisted on precedent and rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Ningjin, Liu Ju, petitioned on behalf of his uncle, the eunuch Yongcheng, for a noble title and posthumous honors, and also asked for an inscribed plaque for a shrine; the Ministry of Rites held to precedent and refused.

sentences.zh: 帝特賜額曰「褒功」，命內閣擬封謚。

translations.literal: The emperor specially granted a plaque reading "Honoring Merit" and ordered the Grand Secretariat to draft ennoblement and posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally granted a plaque bearing the words "Honoring Merit" and ordered the Grand Secretariat to draft titles of ennoblement and posthumous honor.

sentences.zh: 時等言：「即予永誠，將來守邊內臣皆援此陳乞，是變祖宗法自今日始。」

translations.literal: Shi and others said: "If Yongcheng is granted this now, in future border-guarding eunuchs will all cite this in petitioning — it would change the ancestral institutions starting from today.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and the others said, "If Yongcheng is granted this, every eunuch who guards the frontier hereafter will cite this precedent in petition — the ancestral institutions would be altered from this day forward.

sentences.zh: 或言宋童貫封王，時曰：「貫封王在徽宗末年，豈盛世事耶？」

translations.literal: Someone mentioned that Tong Guan of Song was ennobled as king; Shi said: "Tong Guan's kingly ennoblement came at the end of Huizong's reign — is that a matter for a golden age?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone cited how Tong Guan of the Song had been ennobled as a king; Shi replied, "Tong Guan received a royal title only in the last years of Emperor Huizong — is that the sort of thing that happens in an age of good government?"

sentences.zh: 乃寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時每因災變上言，或留中，或下所司，多阻隔，悒悒不得誌。

translations.literal: Whenever calamities occurred Shi would memorialize; sometimes it was kept in the palace, sometimes sent to responsible offices — much was blocked, and he was dejected, unable to fulfill his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever natural disasters struck, Shi would submit memorials; some were kept in the palace, others were passed to the relevant offices — but much was blocked, and he grew dejected, unable to carry out his aims.

sentences.zh: 五年以後，凡七在告，帝輒命醫就視，數遣內臣賜賚。

translations.literal: After the fifth year he took leave seven times in all; each time the emperor ordered physicians to visit him and repeatedly sent eunuchs with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: After the fifth year he went on sick leave seven times in all; each time the emperor sent physicians to attend him and repeatedly dispatched eunuchs bearing gifts.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，以秩滿進少保。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, upon completing his term he was promoted to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year, upon completing his term of service, he was promoted to Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 逾月卒，年六十。

translations.literal: A month later he died, age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚文憲。

translations.literal: Posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor, with posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 時立朝三十年，孜孜奉國，持正存大體，公退未嘗以政語子弟。

translations.literal: Shi served at court thirty years, diligently serving the state, upholding the upright and preserving the larger principles; after leaving office he never spoke of government affairs to his sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: Shi served at court for thirty years, devoting himself tirelessly to the state, upholding integrity and the larger principles of governance; after leaving office he never discussed state affairs with his sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 有所論薦，不使其人知。

translations.literal: When recommending someone, he did not let that person know.
translations.idiomatic: When he recommended someone, he never let that person know.

sentences.zh: 燕居無惰容，服禦儉約，無聲樂之奉，非其義不取，有古大臣風。

translations.literal: In leisurely life he showed no slack countenance; his dress was frugal and plain; he had no music for entertainment; what was not righteous he did not take — he had the bearing of the great ministers of old.
translations.idiomatic: In private life he never showed a slack bearing; his dress was plain and frugal; he kept no musicians for amusement; he accepted nothing that was not right — he had the bearing of the great ministers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 三年，錦衣指揮盧忠令校尉上變，告上皇與少監阮浪、內使王瑤圖復位。

translations.literal: In the third year the Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard Lu Zhong ordered a guard to submit an urgent report, accusing the Retired Emperor, Junior Supervisor Ruan Lang, and inner attendant Wang Yao of plotting restoration.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, Lu Zhong, had a guard submit an urgent report accusing the Retired Emperor, Junior Supervisor Ruan Lang, and the inner attendant Wang Yao of plotting a restoration.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，捕二人下詔獄，窮治之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered; the two were arrested and sent to the imperial prison for thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; the two men were arrested and sent to the imperial prison for exhaustive investigation.

sentences.zh: 忠筮於術者同寅，寅以大義折之，且曰：「此大兇兆，死不足贖。」

translations.literal: Zhong divined with the diviner Tong Yin; Yin refuted him with the greater principle and moreover said: "This is a great evil omen; death would not suffice for atonement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong consulted the diviner Tong Yin; Yin rebuked him on grounds of moral principle and said, "This is a terrible omen — death would not be enough to atone for it.

sentences.zh: 忠懼，佯狂以冀免。

translations.literal: Zhong was afraid and feigned madness hoping to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhong feigned madness in the hope of escaping punishment.

sentences.zh: 輅及中官王誠言於帝曰：「忠病風，無足信，不宜聽妄言，傷大倫。」

translations.literal: Lu and the eunuch Wang Cheng said to the emperor: "Zhong has wind sickness, not worth believing; one should not heed wild talk and harm the great bonds of kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Lu and the eunuch Wang Cheng told the emperor, "Zhong suffers from wind sickness and is not to be believed; wild talk like this should not be heeded, lest it damage the fundamental bonds of kinship.

sentences.zh: 帝意少解。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 乃並下忠獄，坐以他罪，降為事官立功。

translations.literal: Then Zhong was also sent to prison; convicted on other charges, he was demoted to servitor status to earn merit through service.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was then sent to prison as well; convicted on other charges, he was demoted to bondservant status to earn merit through military service.

sentences.zh: 殺瑤，錮浪於獄，事得不竟。

translations.literal: Wang Yao was killed; Ruan Lang was confined in prison; the affair was not pursued to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yao was executed; Ruan Lang was imprisoned; and the affair was not pursued to its conclusion.

sentences.zh: 太子既易，進兵部左侍郎，兼左春坊大學士如故，賜第南薰裏。

translations.literal: After the heir apparent was changed, he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War, continuing concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Left Eastern Pavilion as before, and granted a residence in Nanxun Lane.
translations.idiomatic: After the heir apparent was changed, he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War, continuing as before as Grand Secretary of the Left Eastern Pavilion, and was granted a residence in Nanxun Lane.

sentences.zh: 塞上腴田率為勢豪侵據，輅請核還之軍。

translations.literal: Fertile fields on the frontier were mostly seized by powerful families; Lu requested verification and return to the army.
translations.idiomatic: The fertile fields along the frontier had largely been seized by powerful families; Lu requested that they be verified and returned to military use.

sentences.zh: 開封、鳳陽諸府饑民流濟寧、臨清間，為有司驅逐。

translations.literal: Starving people from Kaifeng, Fengyang, and other prefectures flowed between Jining and Linqing, and were driven away by local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Starving people from Kaifeng, Fengyang, and other prefectures drifted between Jining and Linqing, only to be driven off by local officials.

sentences.zh: 輅憂其為變，請招墾畿內八府閑田，給糧種，民皆有所歸。

translations.literal: Lu feared this would become unrest; he requested recruiting settlers to open idle lands in the eight prefectures within the capital region, providing grain and seed — so the people all had somewhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing this would spark unrest, Lu asked that settlers be recruited to reclaim idle land in the eight prefectures around the capital, with grain and seed provided, so that the people would have somewhere to settle.

sentences.zh: 鐘同、章綸下獄，輅力救得無死。

translations.literal: Zhong Tong and Zhang Lun were sent to prison; Lu worked hard to save them so they did not die.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Tong and Zhang Lun were imprisoned, Lu worked strenuously to save them from execution.

sentences.zh: 《寰宇通志》成，加兼太常卿。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm was completed, he was additionally appointed Vice Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm was completed, he was additionally appointed Vice Director of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 景帝不豫，群臣請建東宮，不許。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing was unwell, the ministers requested establishing the Eastern Palace; he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing fell ill, the ministers petitioned to establish an heir apparent; he refused.

sentences.zh: 將繼奏，輅援筆曰：「陛下宣宗章皇帝之子，當立章皇帝子孫。」

translations.literal: As they were about to continue the memorial, Lu took up the brush and wrote: "Your Majesty is the son of Emperor Xuanzong, styled Zhang; the descendants of Emperor Zhang should be established.
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to continue the memorial, Lu took up the brush and wrote, "Your Majesty is a son of the Xuande Emperor; the heir ought to be chosen from among the Xuande Emperor's descendants.

sentences.zh: 聞者感動。

translations.literal: Those who heard were moved.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 以日暮，奏未入，而是夜石亨輩已迎復上皇。

translations.literal: As it was late in the day the memorial had not been submitted, but that very night Shi Heng and his faction had already welcomed back the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: It was already late in the day and the memorial had not yet been submitted, but that very night Shi Heng and his allies had already restored the Retired Emperor to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明日，王文、于謙等被收，召輅與高谷入便殿，溫旨諭之，命草復位詔。

translations.literal: The next day Wang Wen, Yu Qian, and others were arrested; Lu and Gao Gu were summoned to the informal palace hall, addressed with warm words, and ordered to draft the restoration edict.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wang Wen, Yu Qian, and others were arrested; Shang Lu and Gao Gu were summoned to the informal palace hall, addressed with gracious words, and ordered to draft the restoration edict.

sentences.zh: 亨密語輅，赦文毋別具條款。

translations.literal: Heng spoke secretly to Lu: the amnesty document should not separately list provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng spoke privately to Lu, telling him the amnesty edict should not separately enumerate its provisions.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「舊制也，不敢易。」

translations.literal: Lu said: "It is the old institution; I dare not change it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu replied, "That is the established practice; I dare not alter it.

sentences.zh: 亨輩不悅，諷言官劾輅朋奸，下之獄。

translations.literal: Heng and his faction were displeased; they had censors impeach Lu for factional collusion, and he was sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and his allies were displeased; they had censors impeach Lu for factional collusion, and he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 輅上書自訴《復儲疏》在禮部，可覆驗，不省。

translations.literal: Lu submitted a memorial pleading his case: the "Restoration of the Heir Apparent Memorial" was on file at the Ministry of Rites and could be verified — the emperor paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu submitted a memorial in his own defense, noting that his "Memorial on Restoring the Heir Apparent" was on file at the Ministry of Rites and could be checked — but the emperor paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 中官興安稍解之，帝愈怒。

translations.literal: The eunuch Xing'an slightly interceded for him; the emperor grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Xing'an tried mildly to intercede for him, but the emperor only grew angrier.

sentences.zh: 安曰：「向者此輩創議南遷，不審置陛下何地。」

translations.literal: An said: "In the past these men first proposed moving the capital south — they gave no thought to where Your Majesty would be placed.
translations.idiomatic: Xing'an said, "These men were the ones who first proposed moving the capital south — they gave no thought to where Your Majesty would be left.

sentences.zh: 帝意漸釋，乃斥為民。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger gradually eased; Lu was then dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger gradually subsided, and Lu was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 然帝每獨念「輅，朕所取士，嘗與姚夔侍東宮」，不忍棄之。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor often thought privately: "Lu is a jinshi I personally selected; he once attended the Eastern Palace together with Yao Kui" — and could not bear to abandon him entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor often thought to himself, "Lu is a jinshi I personally chose; he once served the Eastern Palace together with Yao Kui" — and could not bear to cast him aside entirely.

sentences.zh: 以忌者，竟不復用。

translations.literal: Because of those who envied him, in the end he was never reemployed.
translations.idiomatic: But because of those who envied him, he was never reemployed.

sentences.zh: 明年，彗星見，給事中董旻、御史胡深等劾不職大臣，並及輅。

translations.literal: The next year a comet appeared; Supervising Secretary Dong Min, Censor Hu Shen, and others impeached negligent great ministers, including Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year a comet appeared; the supervising secretary Dong Min, the censor Hu Shen, and others impeached negligent senior ministers, Shang Lu among them.

sentences.zh: 御史林誠詆輅曾與易儲，不宜用，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Censor Lin Cheng slandered Lu for having once changed the heir apparent and said he ought not be employed; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Lin Cheng attacked Lu for having once supported a change of heir and argued he should not be employed; the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 輅因求罷。

translations.literal: Lu therefore requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Lu therefore asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命廷鞫諸言者，欲加重譴。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered a court trial for those who had spoken, intending to impose heavier punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and ordered a court trial of those who had spoken out, intending to impose heavier punishment.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「臣嘗請優容言者，今論臣反責之，如公論何？」

translations.literal: Lu said: "Your subject once requested leniency for those who speak out; now because of accusations against me You would punish them — what of public opinion?
translations.idiomatic: Lu said, "Your subject once asked that those who speak out be treated with forbearance; now because of accusations against me You would punish them — what becomes of public opinion?

sentences.zh: 帝悅，旻等各予杖復職。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased; Dong Min and the others each received beating with the rod and were restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased; Dong Min and the others each received a beating with the rod and were restored to office.

sentences.zh: 尋進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 久之，進戶部。

translations.literal: After a long while he advanced to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 《宋元通鑒綱目》成，改兼文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: When the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror from Song and Yuan was completed, he was transferred to serve concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror from Song and Yuan was completed, he was made Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 皇太子立，加太子少保，進吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was established, he was additionally made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was established, he was additionally made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十三年進謹身殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall.

sentences.zh: 輅為人，平粹簡重，寬厚有容，至臨大事，決大議，毅然莫能奪。

translations.literal: Lu as a man was even-tempered, pure, simple and weighty, generous and tolerant; but when facing great affairs and deciding great questions, he was resolute and none could sway him.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Lu was even-tempered, upright, and dignified, generous and forbearing; yet when great affairs arose and weighty questions had to be decided, he was resolute and could not be moved.

sentences.zh: 仁壽太后莊戶與民爭田，帝欲徙民塞外。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Renshou's estate fought with commoners over fields; the emperor wished to relocate the people beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Renshou's estate disputed land with commoners, the emperor wished to relocate the people beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「天子以天下為家，安用皇莊為？」

translations.literal: Lu said: "The Son of Heaven takes all under Heaven as his home — what need is there for imperial estates?
translations.idiomatic: Lu said, "The Son of Heaven takes all under Heaven as his home — what need is there for imperial estates?

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮門災，工部請采木川、湖。

translations.literal: When the Qianqing Palace gate suffered fire, the Ministry of Works requested timber procurement in Sichuan and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: When fire destroyed the gate of the Qianqing Palace, the Ministry of Works requested timber from Sichuan and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 輅言宜少緩，以存警畏，從之。

translations.literal: Lu said it should be somewhat delayed, to preserve a sense of vigilance and awe; the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Lu argued that the work should be delayed somewhat, to preserve a sense of vigilance and awe; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 悼恭太子薨，帝以繼嗣為憂。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Daogong died, the emperor was troubled about succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Daogong died, the emperor was deeply troubled about the succession.

sentences.zh: 紀妃生皇子，六歲矣，左右畏萬貴妃，莫敢言。

translations.literal: Consort Ji had borne a prince who was now six years old; those around him feared Consort Wan and no one dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Ji had borne a prince who was now six years old, but those around the emperor feared Consort Wan and no one dared speak of it.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃聞於帝。

translations.literal: After a long time the emperor finally heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long time did the emperor finally learn of it.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，欲宣示外廷，遣中官至內閣諭意。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and wished to announce it to the outer court; he sent a eunuch to the Grand Secretariat to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed and wished to announce it to the outer court; he sent a eunuch to the Grand Secretariat to convey his intent.

sentences.zh: 輅請敕禮部擬上皇子名，於是廷臣相率稱賀。

translations.literal: Lu requested an edict ordering the Ministry of Rites to draft a name for the prince; thereupon court ministers successively offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Lu asked that an edict be issued ordering the Ministry of Rites to draft a name for the prince; thereupon the court ministers one after another offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝即命皇子出見廷臣。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered the prince brought out to meet the court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered the prince brought out to meet the court ministers.

sentences.zh: 越數日，帝復禦文華殿，皇子侍，召見輅及諸閣臣。

translations.literal: Several days later the emperor again held audience at the Wenhua Hall with the prince in attendance, and summoned Lu and the other grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the emperor again held audience at the Wenhua Hall with the prince in attendance and summoned Shang Lu and the other grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 輅頓首曰：「陛下踐祚十年，儲副未立，天下引領望久矣。

translations.literal: Lu kowtowed and said: "Your Majesty has occupied the throne ten years without establishing an heir apparent; all under Heaven have long craned their necks in anticipation.
translations.idiomatic: Lu kowtowed and said, "Your Majesty has reigned ten years without establishing an heir apparent; the whole realm has long waited in eager anticipation.

sentences.zh: 當即立為皇太子，安中外心。」

translations.literal: He should immediately be established as Crown Prince, to settle the hearts within and without.
translations.idiomatic: He should be established as crown prince at once, to reassure the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded in assent.

sentences.zh: 是冬，遂立皇子為皇太子。

translations.literal: That winter the prince was duly established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the prince was duly established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，帝召見皇子留宮中，而紀妃仍居西內。

translations.literal: Initially, the emperor summoned and saw the prince, keeping him in the palace, while Consort Ji still resided in the Western Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor summoned the prince, kept him in the palace, and Consort Ji remained in the Western Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 輅恐有他患，難顯言，偕同官上疏曰：「皇子聰明岐嶷，國本攸系。

translations.literal: Lu feared some other harm and found it hard to speak plainly; together with his colleagues he submitted a memorial saying: "The prince is intelligent and exceptional — the foundation of the state depends on him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu feared some other trouble and could not speak openly; he joined his colleagues in a memorial: "The prince is bright and precocious, and the succession of the realm hangs upon him.

sentences.zh: 重以貴妃保護，恩逾己出。

translations.literal: Moreover, with the imperial consort's protection, the favor shown him exceeds what one would show one's own child.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, under the imperial consort's care, the kindness shown him surpasses even that owed to one's own son.

sentences.zh: 但外議謂皇子母因病別居，久不得見。

translations.literal: But outside opinion holds that the prince's mother, because of illness, lives apart and has long been unable to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet public talk holds that the prince's mother, ill and living apart, has long been unable to see him.

sentences.zh: 宜移就近所，俾母子朝夕相接，而皇子仍藉撫育於貴妃，宗社幸甚。」

translations.literal: She should be moved to a nearby residence, so that mother and son may meet morning and evening, while the prince still relies on the imperial consort for nurture — great fortune for altars and state.
translations.idiomatic: She should be moved nearby so mother and son may meet daily, while the prince continues to be raised under the imperial consort's care — a great blessing for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 由是紀妃遷永壽宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon Consort Ji was moved to the Palace of Eternal Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Consort Ji was moved to the Palace of Eternal Longevity.

sentences.zh: 逾月，妃病篤。

translations.literal: After more than a month, the consort's illness grew grave.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the consort's illness turned critical.

sentences.zh: 輅請曰：「如有不諱，禮宜從厚。」

translations.literal: Lu requested: "If the worst should befall, the rites ought to be full and generous.
translations.idiomatic: Lu petitioned: "Should the worst come to pass, the funeral rites ought to be conducted with full honor.

sentences.zh: 且請命司禮監奉皇子，過妃宮問視，及制衰服行禮。

translations.literal: He also requested that the Directorate of Ceremonial be ordered to accompany the prince to visit the consort's palace, and that mourning garments be made for him to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the Directorate of Ceremonial escort the prince to the consort's quarters to inquire after her, and that mourning garments be prepared so he could perform the proper rites.

sentences.zh: 帝皆是之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every request.

sentences.zh: 帝將復郕王位號，下廷議。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to restore the title of Prince of Cheng and submitted the matter to court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor intended to restore the Prince of Cheng's title and submitted the matter for court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 輅極言王有社稷功，位號當復，帝意遂決。

translations.literal: Lu spoke at length that the prince had merit to the altars and state, and that his title ought to be restored — the emperor's mind was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: Lu argued forcefully that the prince had served the realm and deserved restoration of his title, and the emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 帝建玉皇閣於宮北，命內臣執事，禮與郊祀等，輅等爭罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor built the Jade Emperor Pavilion north of the palace, ordered eunuchs to officiate, with rites equal to suburban sacrifice — Lu and the others protested until it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built the Jade Emperor Pavilion north of the palace, put eunuchs in charge, and planned rites on a par with the suburban sacrifice; Lu and his colleagues protested until the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 黑眚見，疏弭災八事，曰：番僧國師法王，毋濫賜印章；

translations.literal: A black omen appeared; he memorialized eight items to avert disaster, saying: Tibetan monks, national preceptors, and dharma kings — do not lavishly bestow seals upon them;
translations.idiomatic: When a dark omen appeared, he submitted eight proposals to avert calamity: do not lavish seals on Tibetan monks, national preceptors, and dharma kings;

sentences.zh: 四方常貢外，勿受玩好；

translations.literal: apart from regular tribute from the four quarters, do not accept curios and delights;
translations.idiomatic: apart from regular tribute from the four directions, accept no curios or luxuries;

sentences.zh: 許諸臣直言；

translations.literal: allow officials to speak frankly;
translations.idiomatic: permit officials to speak plainly;

sentences.zh: 分遣部使慮囚，省冤獄；

translations.literal: dispatch ministers in divisions to review prisoners and reduce unjust imprisonments;
translations.idiomatic: send out ministers in turn to review prisoners and reduce wrongful convictions;

sentences.zh: 停不急營造，實三邊軍儲；

translations.literal: halt non-urgent construction, and fill the grain stores of the three frontiers;
translations.idiomatic: suspend nonessential construction and fill the grain stores on the three frontiers;

sentences.zh: 守沿邊關隘；

translations.literal: hold the passes and barriers along the borders;
translations.idiomatic: hold the frontier passes and barriers;

sentences.zh: 設雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: establish a grand coordinator for Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: establish a grand coordinator for Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔褒納。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict praising and accepting it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with a gracious edict of praise and acceptance.

sentences.zh: 中官汪直之督西廠也，數興大獄。

translations.literal: When the eunuch Wang Zhi supervised the Western Depot, he repeatedly stirred up major cases.
translations.idiomatic: While the eunuch Wang Zhi oversaw the Western Depot, he repeatedly launched major prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 輅率同官條直十一罪，言：「陛下委聽斷於直，直又寄耳目於群小如韋瑛輩。

translations.literal: Lu led his colleagues in listing eleven crimes of Zhi, saying: "Your Majesty has entrusted judgments to Zhi, and Zhi in turn places his eyes and ears in petty men like Wei Ying and his kind.
translations.idiomatic: Lu led his colleagues in listing eleven crimes against Zhi, saying: "Your Majesty has entrusted judgment to Zhi, and Zhi in turn relies on petty men such as Wei Ying for his eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 皆自言承密旨，得顓刑殺，擅作威福，賊虐善良。

translations.literal: They all claim to carry secret edicts, obtain exclusive power to punish and kill, arrogate authority and bestow favors, and abuse the good and meek.
translations.idiomatic: They all claim secret edicts, wield exclusive power over life and death, abuse their authority for private gain, and prey upon the innocent.

sentences.zh: 陛下若謂擿奸禁亂，法不得已，則前此數年，何以帖然無事？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty considers that uncovering treachery and suppressing disorder makes the law unavoidable, then in the several years before this, why was all at ease and without incident?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty holds that uncovering treachery and suppressing disorder leave no choice but harsh law, then why were the preceding years so tranquil and untroubled?

sentences.zh: 且曹欽之變，由逯杲刺事激成，可為懲鑒。

translations.literal: Moreover, Cao Qin's rebellion was provoked by Lu Gao's secret investigation — it may serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Cao Qin's uprising was provoked by Lu Gao's secret investigations — a lesson that should not be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 自直用事，士大夫不安其職，商賈不安於途，庶民不安於業，若不亟去，天下安危未可知也。」

translations.literal: Since Zhi came to power, scholar-officials cannot rest in their posts, merchants cannot rest on the roads, and common people cannot rest in their trades — if he is not removed promptly, whether the realm will be safe or in peril cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhi took power, officials cannot perform their duties in peace, merchants cannot travel in peace, and common people cannot work in peace; if he is not removed at once, the realm's safety is impossible to foresee.

sentences.zh: 帝慍曰：「用一內豎，何遽危天下，誰主此奏者？」

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily: "Employ one inner attendant, and how could the realm suddenly be imperiled — who drafted this memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in anger: "Because I employ one palace eunuch, how could the realm suddenly be endangered? Who drafted this memorial?"

sentences.zh: 命太監懷恩傳旨，詰責厲甚。

translations.literal: He ordered the eunuch Huai'en to convey the edict and sternly rebuke them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the eunuch Huai'en to deliver the imperial message and rebuke them with unusual severity.

sentences.zh: 輅正色曰：「朝臣無大小，有罪皆請旨逮問，直擅抄沒三品以上京官。

translations.literal: Lu said with a stern countenance: "Whether court officials are great or small, if guilty they all request imperial order before arrest and inquiry — Zhi on his own authority raids and confiscates third-rank and above capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Lu answered sternly: "Court officials great and small, when guilty, are all arrested only by imperial order — yet Zhi on his own authority raids and seizes third-rank capital officials and above.

sentences.zh: 大同、宣府，邊城要害，守備俄頃不可缺。

translations.literal: Datong and Xuanfu — border strongholds of vital importance — their garrisons cannot be left vacant even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Datong and Xuanfu are vital frontier strongholds whose garrisons cannot stand empty even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 直一日械數人。

translations.literal: In a single day Zhi shackles several men.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day Zhi puts several men in fetters.

sentences.zh: 南京，祖宗根本地，留守大臣，直擅收捕。

translations.literal: Nanjing — the ancestral foundation of the dynasty — the grand ministers on garrison duty, Zhi on his own authority arrests them.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing is the dynasty's ancestral foundation, yet Zhi on his own authority arrests the grand ministers left to guard it.

sentences.zh: 諸近侍在帝左右，直輒易置。

translations.literal: The close attendants at the emperor's side — Zhi readily replaces them.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants at the emperor's side — Zhi replaces them at will.

sentences.zh: 直不去，天下安得無危？」

translations.literal: If Zhi does not go, how can the realm not be imperiled?
translations.idiomatic: If Zhi is not removed, how can the realm remain safe?

sentences.zh: 萬安、劉珝、劉吉亦俱對，引義慷慨，恩等屈服。

translations.literal: Wan An, Liu Yu, and Liu Ji also all responded, citing principle with passion; Huai'en and the others yielded.
