translations.idiomatic: Wan An, Liu Yu, and Liu Ji also spoke up, invoking principle with passionate force, and Huai'en and the others were forced to yield.

sentences.zh: 輅顧同列謝曰：「諸公皆為國如此，輅復何憂。」

translations.literal: Lu turned to his colleagues and said in thanks: "You gentlemen all serve the state thus — what need has Lu to worry?
translations.idiomatic: Lu turned to his colleagues and said with gratitude: "You gentlemen have all served the state like this — what more need Lu worry about?

sentences.zh: 會九卿項忠等亦劾直，是日遂罷西廠。

translations.literal: At the same time the nine ministers led by Xiang Zhong also impeached Zhi, and that day the Western Depot was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the nine ministers, led by Xiang Zhong, also impeached Zhi, and that day the Western Depot was abolished.

sentences.zh: 直雖不視廠事，寵幸如故。

translations.literal: Although Zhi no longer managed depot affairs, his favor and privilege remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zhi no longer oversaw the depot, his favor at court remained undiminished.

sentences.zh: 譖輅嘗納指揮楊曄賄，欲脫其罪。

translations.literal: He slandered Lu, saying he had once accepted a bribe from Commander Yang Ye to secure his acquittal.
translations.idiomatic: He slandered Lu, claiming he had once taken a bribe from the commander Yang Ye to secure his acquittal.

sentences.zh: 輅不自安，而御史戴縉復頌直功，請復西廠，輅遂力求去。

translations.literal: Lu felt uneasy, and when Censor Dai Jin again praised Zhi's merit and requested restoration of the Western Depot, Lu therefore strove to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Lu grew uneasy, and when Censor Dai Jin again praised Zhi's achievements and petitioned to restore the Western Depot, Lu pressed hard to resign.

sentences.zh: 詔加少保，賜敕馳傳歸。

translations.literal: An edict added Junior Guardian rank and granted him an imperial letter to return home by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to Junior Guardian and granted him an imperial letter to return home by express relay.

sentences.zh: 輅既去，士大夫益俯首事直，無敢與抗者矣。

translations.literal: After Lu departed, scholar-officials bowed their heads even lower in serving Zhi — none dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu left, officials bowed even lower before Zhi, and none dared stand against him.

sentences.zh: 錢溥嘗以不遷官，作《禿婦傳》以譏輅。

translations.literal: Qian Pu once, for not being promoted, wrote "Biography of the Bald Wife" to ridicule Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Pu, passed over for promotion, once wrote "Biography of the Bald Wife" to mock Lu.

sentences.zh: 高瑤請復景帝位號，黎淳疏駁，極詆輅。

translations.literal: Gao Yao requested restoration of Emperor Jing's title; Li Chun memorialized in rebuttal, vehemently denouncing Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yao petitioned to restore Emperor Jing's title; Li Chun submitted a rebuttal that fiercely denounced Lu.

sentences.zh: 輅皆不為較，待之如平時。

translations.literal: Lu never contested any of this and treated them as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Lu never took offense and treated them as he always had.

sentences.zh: 萬貴妃重輅名，出父像，屬為贊，遺金帛甚厚。

translations.literal: Consort Wan esteemed Lu's reputation; she produced her father's portrait and entrusted him to write an encomium, sending gold and silks in great quantity.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wan respected Lu's reputation, produced her father's portrait, and asked him to compose an encomium, sending a lavish gift of gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 輅力辭，使者告以妃意。

translations.literal: Lu forcefully declined; the envoy told him of the consort's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu firmly declined; the envoy relayed the consort's wishes.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「非上命，不敢承也。」

translations.literal: Lu said: "Without an imperial command, I dare not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Lu said: "Without an imperial command, I dare not accept.

sentences.zh: 貴妃不悅，輅終不顧。

translations.literal: The consort was displeased — Lu ultimately paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was displeased, but Lu never yielded.

sentences.zh: 其和而有執如此。

translations.literal: His harmonious yet resolute character was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his manner — conciliatory, yet firm when it mattered.

sentences.zh: 及謝政，劉吉過之，見其子孫林立，嘆曰：「吉與公同事歷年，未嘗見公筆下妄殺一人，宜天之報公厚。」

translations.literal: After he retired from office, Liu Ji visited him and, seeing his sons and grandsons standing in ranks, sighed: "Ji has served with you for years and has never seen you, by your own hand, wrongly put anyone to death — Heaven's reward to you is fittingly generous.
translations.idiomatic: After he retired, Liu Ji visited him and, seeing sons and grandsons standing about in ranks, sighed: "I have served with you for years and never saw you, by your own hand, put an innocent person to death — no wonder Heaven has rewarded you so richly.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「正不敢使朝廷妄殺一人耳。」

translations.literal: Lu said: "It is precisely that I dared not let the court wrongly put anyone to death."
translations.idiomatic: Lu said: "It is precisely because I never dared let the court put an innocent person to death."

sentences.zh: 居十年卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He lived ten years and died at age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He lived ten years in retirement and died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous name Wenyì.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wenyì.

sentences.zh: 子良臣，成化初進士，官翰林侍講。

translations.literal: His son Liangchen, a jinshi of the early Chenghua reign, served as Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liangchen, a jinshi in the early Chenghua reign, served as a Hanlin reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 劉定之，字主靜，永新人。

translations.literal: Liu Dingzhi, style name Zhujing, was a native of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dingzhi, styled Zhujing, was a native of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 幼有異稟。

translations.literal: In childhood he had exceptional endowment.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he showed unusual gifts.

sentences.zh: 父授之書，日誦數千言。

translations.literal: When his father taught him books, he daily recited several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: When his father taught him to read, he could recite several thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 不令作文，一日偶見所為《祀竈文》。

translations.literal: He was not made to compose essays; one day his father happened to see what he had written — the "Stove God Text."
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet been taught to write essays when one day his father happened upon a "Stove God Text" he had composed.

sentences.zh: 大異之。

translations.literal: His father was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: His father was astonished.

sentences.zh: 舉正統元年會試第一，殿試及第，授編修。

translations.literal: He took first place in the metropolitan examination of the first year of Zhengtong and passed the palace examination, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the metropolitan examination of the first year of Zhengtong, passed the palace examination, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 京城大水，應詔陳十事，言：「號令宜出大公，裁以至正，不可茍且數易。

translations.literal: When the capital suffered great flood, he responded to the edict with ten items, saying: "Orders and proclamations should proceed from the greatest public good, trimmed to utmost correctness — they must not be casually and repeatedly changed.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was struck by severe flooding, he responded to an imperial edict with ten proposals: "Edicts should proceed from the broad public good, trimmed to what is right, and must not be changed lightly and often.

sentences.zh: 公卿侍從，當數召見，察其才能心術而進退之。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers in attendance should frequently be summoned, their talent and inner disposition observed, and they should be promoted or dismissed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, ministers, and attendants should be summoned often, their ability and character assessed, and they should be promoted or dismissed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 降人散處京畿者，宜漸移之南方。

translations.literal: Those who surrendered and are scattered in the capital region should gradually be moved southward.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered peoples scattered about the capital region should gradually be resettled in the south.

sentences.zh: 郡縣職以京朝官補，使叠相出入，內外無畸重。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county posts should be filled by capital officials in rotation, so that posts alternate between inner and outer service without lopsided weight.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county posts should be filled by capital officials in rotation, so that service alternates between court and provinces without either side overweighted.

sentences.zh: 薦舉之法，不當拘五品以上。

translations.literal: The method of recommendation ought not to be limited to those of fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: The rules of recommendation should not be restricted to officials of fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 可仿唐制，朝臣遷秩，舉一人自代，吏部籍其名而簡用之。

translations.literal: The Tang system may be imitated: when court ministers are transferred in rank, each recommends one to replace himself, and the Ministry of Personnel records the names and selects for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang practice may be revived: when a court minister is transferred, he should recommend one successor, and the Ministry of Personnel should keep a register of names and select from it.

sentences.zh: 武臣子孫，教以韜略。

translations.literal: The sons and grandsons of military officers should be taught military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The sons and grandsons of military officers should be trained in strategy and tactics.

sentences.zh: 守令牧養為先務，毋徒取幹辦。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates should make nurturing the people their first duty, not merely seek efficiency in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates should put nurturing the people first, not merely prize administrative efficiency.

sentences.zh: 群臣遭喪，乞永罷起復以教孝。

translations.literal: When ministers suffer bereavement, permanently abolish the practice of resuming office to teach filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers suffer a parent's death, permanently abolish the practice of resuming office from mourning, so as to teach filial piety.

sentences.zh: 僧尼蠹國當嚴絕。

translations.literal: Monks and nuns who harm the state should be strictly barred.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and nuns who drain the state should be strictly suppressed.

sentences.zh: 富民輸粟授官者，有犯宜追奪。」

translations.literal: Rich men who buy offices by submitting grain — if they commit offenses, their appointments should be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy men who buy office by submitting grain should have their appointments revoked if they commit offenses.

sentences.zh: 疏入留中。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and was retained at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received and retained at court.

sentences.zh: 十三年，弟寅之與鄉人相訐，辭連定之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, his younger brother Yinzhi quarreled with a fellow townsman, and the lawsuit implicated Dingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his younger brother Yinzhi quarreled with a fellow townsman, and the case implicated Dingzhi.

sentences.zh: 下獄，得白。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned but cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned but later cleared.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，進侍講。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，復上言十事，曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing took the throne, he again submitted ten items, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing took the throne, he again submitted ten proposals:

sentences.zh: 自古如晉懷、湣、宋徽、欽，皆因邊塞外破，藩鎮內潰，救援不集，馴致播遷。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, such as Jin Huai, Min, Song Hui, and Qin — all because the outer frontier was broken and inner fiefs rebelled, aid did not gather, and they were driven step by step to wander in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, emperors such as Jin Huai and Min, and Song Hui and Qin, all fell because the outer frontier collapsed, inner garrisons rebelled, relief failed to arrive, and they were driven step by step into exile.

sentences.zh: 未有若今日以天下之大，數十萬之師，奉上皇於漠北，委以與寇者也。

translations.literal: Never has there been anything like today — with so great a realm and an army of hundreds of thousands, to hold the Former Emperor in the northern wastes and hand him over to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Never before has a realm so vast, with an army of hundreds of thousands, held the former emperor captive in the northern wastes and handed him over to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋遭禍亂，棄故土，偏安一隅，尚能奮於既衰，以禦方張之敵。

translations.literal: Jin and Song, when they met calamity and disorder, abandoned their old lands and clung to one corner in partial security, yet still could rouse themselves in decline to resist enemies on the rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin and Song met calamity, they abandoned their old lands and clung to a corner of the realm, yet even in decline they could still rouse themselves to resist enemies on the rise.

sentences.zh: 未有若今日也先乘勝直抵都城。

translations.literal: Never has there been anything like today, when Esen, riding victory, pressed straight to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Never before has an enemy such as Esen, riding victory, pressed straight to the capital as today.

sentences.zh: 以師武臣之眾，既不能奮武以破賊，又不能約和以迎駕。

translations.literal: With so numerous an army of martial officers, they could neither exert martial valor to break the bandits, nor negotiate peace to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: With so vast an army of martial officers, they could neither fight boldly to break the enemy nor negotiate peace to welcome the emperor home.

sentences.zh: 聽其自來而自去者也。

translations.literal: They merely let the enemy come of his own accord and leave of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: They simply let the enemy come and go as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 國勢之弱，雖非旦夕所能強，豈可不思自強之術而力行之。

translations.literal: The state's strength, though it cannot be made strong in a morning or evening, how can we not think of methods of self-strengthening and earnestly put them into practice?
translations.idiomatic: The realm's weakness cannot be remedied overnight, yet how can we fail to devise methods of self-strengthening and put them earnestly into practice?

sentences.zh: 臣愚敢略陳所見。

translations.literal: This subject, in his dullness, dares briefly to set forth what he has observed.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant dares briefly set forth what he has observed.

sentences.zh: 近日京軍之戰，但知堅壁持重，而不能用奇制勝。

translations.literal: In recent battles of the capital armies, they only knew to hold fast behind walls and maintain weight, but could not use stratagem to gain victory.
translations.idiomatic: In recent battles the capital armies knew only to hold fast behind walls, and could not use stratagem to win.

sentences.zh: 至前敗而後不救，左出而右不隨。

translations.literal: When the forward line was defeated the rear did not rescue; when the left column went out the right did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the vanguard was beaten the rear did not rescue it; when the left wing advanced the right did not follow.

sentences.zh: 謂宜仿宋吳玠、吳璘三疊陣法，互相倚恃，叠為救護。

translations.literal: It would be appropriate to imitate the Song generals Wu Jie and Wu Lin's triple-array formation — mutual reliance, layered rescue.
translations.idiomatic: They should adopt the triple-array formation of the Song generals Wu Jie and Wu Lin, relying on one another in layered support and rescue.

sentences.zh: 至鐵騎沖突，必資刀斧以制之。

translations.literal: When iron cavalry charges, one must rely on halberds and axes to check them.
translations.idiomatic: Against charging iron cavalry, halberds and axes are essential to check them.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀破安祿山八萬騎，用千人執長刀如墻而進。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi broke An Lushan's eighty thousand horsemen by having a thousand men wield long sabers and advance like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi broke An Lushan's eighty thousand horsemen by advancing a thousand men with long sabers like a moving wall.

sentences.zh: 韓世忠破兀术拐子馬，用五百人執長斧，上揕人胸，下斫馬足。

translations.literal: Han Shizhong broke Wuzhu's iron-linked cavalry by using five hundred men with long axes — thrusting upward at men's chests, cutting downward at horses' legs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong broke Wuzhu's linked-cavalry formation with five hundred men wielding long axes, thrusting upward at riders' chests and cutting downward at horses' legs.

sentences.zh: 是刀斧揮霍便捷，優於火槍也。

translations.literal: Thus halberds and axes, wielded freely and readily, are superior to fire lances.
translations.idiomatic: Halberds and axes, wielded swiftly at close range, are more effective than fire lances.

sentences.zh: 紫荊、居庸二關，名為關塞，實則坦途。

translations.literal: The two passes Zijing and Juyong — named border fortresses, but in reality open roads.
translations.idiomatic: The Zijing and Juyong passes are called frontier barriers, but in truth they are open roads.

sentences.zh: 今宜增兵士，繕亭障，塞蹊隧。

translations.literal: Now soldiers should be increased, watchtowers and barriers repaired, and hidden paths blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers should be increased, watchtowers and barriers repaired, and hidden paths sealed off.

sentences.zh: 陸則縱橫掘塹，名曰「地網」。

translations.literal: On land, dig trenches crisscrossing — called "earth nets."
translations.idiomatic: On land, trenches should be dug in crisscross patterns, called "earth nets."

sentences.zh: 水則氵豬泉令深，名曰「水櫃」。

translations.literal: In water, deepen the stagnant pools — called "water caskets."
translations.idiomatic: In waterways, pools should be deepened, called "water caskets."

sentences.zh: 或多植榆柳，以制奔突，或多招鄉勇，以助官軍。

translations.literal: Or plant many elms and willows to check sudden charges; or recruit many local braves to assist the official army.
translations.idiomatic: Plant elms and willows to check sudden charges, or recruit local militia to assist the regular army.

sentences.zh: 此皆古所嘗為，已有明效。

translations.literal: These are all things done in antiquity, with proven effect.
translations.idiomatic: All these measures were used in antiquity and have proven effective.

sentences.zh: 往者奉使之臣，充以驛人駔夫，招釁啟戎，職此之故。

translations.literal: Former envoys on tribute missions were filled out with relay runners and grooms — provoking incidents and opening hostilities; their office was the cause of this.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, tribute envoys were staffed with relay runners and grooms, provoking incidents and inviting war — this was the root of the trouble.

sentences.zh: 今宜擇內蘊忠悃，外工專對，若陸賈、富弼其人者，使備正介之選，庶不失辭辱國。

translations.literal: Now one should select men who inwardly harbor loyal sincerity and outwardly excel at specialized diplomatic replies, such as Lu Jia or Fu Bi, to stand ready for selection as chief envoys, so that the state will not suffer disgrace through unworthy words.
translations.idiomatic: Now is the time to choose envoys who are inwardly loyal and outwardly skilled in diplomatic discourse—men in the mold of Lu Jia or Fu Bi—to fill the ranks of chief ambassadors, so the realm is not shamed by words unworthy of the occasion.

sentences.zh: 臣於上皇朝，乞徙漠北降人，知謀短淺，未蒙采納。

translations.literal: I, your minister, in the reign of the Retired Emperor, begged to relocate the surrendered people from beyond the northern deserts. Recognizing that my plan was shallow and short-sighted, it was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Retired Emperor's reign I petitioned to relocate the surrendered peoples of the northern steppe. My plan was too shallow to win acceptance, and it was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 比乘國釁，奔歸故土，寇掠畿甸者屢見告矣。

translations.literal: Recently, taking advantage of national discord, they have fled back to their native lands; reports of their raiding and pillaging the capital region have repeatedly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Lately they have seized on national turmoil to flee home, and we have received repeated reports of their raiding the capital districts.

sentences.zh: 宜乘大兵聚集時，遷之南方。

translations.literal: They should be relocated to the south while the main army is assembled.
translations.idiomatic: They should be moved south while the main forces are gathered.

sentences.zh: 使與中國兵民相錯雜，以牽制而變化之。

translations.literal: Let them be intermixed with Chinese soldiers and civilians, so as to control and transform them.
translations.idiomatic: Intermingle them with Chinese troops and commoners so they can be controlled and gradually assimilated.

sentences.zh: 且可省俸給，減漕免，其事甚便。

translations.literal: Moreover, salary payments can be saved and canal transport levies reduced — the matter would be very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: It would also save salary outlays and reduce grain-transport burdens—a highly practical measure.

sentences.zh: 天下農出粟，女出布，以養兵也。

translations.literal: Under Heaven, farmers produce grain and women produce cloth to support the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Across the realm, farmers grow grain and women weave cloth to sustain the army.

sentences.zh: 兵受粟於倉，受布於庫，以衛國也。

translations.literal: Soldiers receive grain from the granaries and cloth from the storehouses to defend the state.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers draw grain from the granaries and cloth from the storehouses in order to defend the state.

sentences.zh: 向者兵士受粟布於公門，納月錢於私室。

translations.literal: Formerly soldiers received grain and cloth at the public gates but paid monthly fees at private residences.
translations.idiomatic: In the past soldiers collected their grain and cloth at the public gate, then paid monthly fees in private quarters.

sentences.zh: 於是手不習擊刺之法，足不習進退之宜。

translations.literal: Thus their hands did not practice thrust-and-strike techniques, nor their feet the proper arts of advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Their hands never learned the arts of thrust and parry; their feet never learned the proper drill of advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 第轉貨為商，執技為工，而以工商所得，補納月錢。

translations.literal: They merely turned goods as merchants or wielded skills as craftsmen, using earnings from commerce and craft to cover their monthly payments.
translations.idiomatic: They simply traded as merchants or worked as craftsmen, using their commercial and artisan earnings to meet the monthly payments.

sentences.zh: 民之膏血，兵之氣力，皆變為金銀以惠奸宄。

translations.literal: The people's vital essence and the soldiers' strength all turned into gold and silver to benefit villains and evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: The people's lifeblood and the soldiers' strength were converted into gold and silver that enriched scoundrels and criminals.

sentences.zh: 一旦率以臨敵，如驅羊拒狼，幾何其不敗也！

translations.literal: Once led against the enemy, it would be like driving sheep to resist wolves — how could they not be defeated!
translations.idiomatic: If such men were led into battle, it would be like driving sheep against wolves—how could defeat not follow?

sentences.zh: 今宜痛革其弊，一新簡練之政，將帥踵舊習者誅毋赦。

translations.literal: Now these abuses should be radically reformed and training discipline wholly renewed; generals who follow old corrupt practices should be executed without mercy.
translations.idiomatic: These abuses must be ruthlessly uprooted and military training wholly reformed; any commander who persists in the old corrupt ways should be executed without pardon.

sentences.zh: 如是而兵威不振者，未之有也。

translations.literal: If this were done and military might still did not revive, it would never have happened.
translations.idiomatic: Do this, and military power will surely be restored—there has never been a case where it failed.

sentences.zh: 守令朘民，猶將帥之剝兵也。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates who squeeze the people are like generals who strip their soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When prefects and magistrates squeeze the people, it is no different from generals stripping their own troops.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴糾考，慎黜陟。

translations.literal: Corruption investigations should be strict and promotions and dismissals carefully weighed.
translations.idiomatic: Corruption inquiries should be rigorous, and appointments and dismissals should be made with care.

sentences.zh: 犯贓者舉主與其罰，然後貪墨者寡，薦舉者慎，民安而邦本固矣。

translations.literal: When someone guilty of embezzling is punished, his recommender should share the penalty — then the corrupt would be few, those who recommend would be cautious, the people would be at peace, and the foundation of the state would be firm.
translations.idiomatic: When an embezzler is punished, his patron should share the penalty. Then the corrupt would be fewer, recommenders more cautious, the people secure, and the state's foundation firm.

sentences.zh: 古販繒屠狗之夫，俱足助成帝業。

translations.literal: In antiquity, men who sold silk or butchered dogs were both sufficient to help accomplish imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, men who sold silk or butchered dogs were quite capable of helping build an empire.

sentences.zh: 今于謙、楊善亦非出自將門。

translations.literal: Today Yu Qian and Yang Shan also did not come from military families.
translations.idiomatic: Today, neither Yu Qian nor Yang Shan came from military families.

sentences.zh: 然將能知將，宜令各舉所知，不限門閥。

translations.literal: Yet a general can recognize a general; each should be ordered to recommend those he knows, without limiting by family status.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a general knows a general when he sees one; each commander should be ordered to recommend men he knows, without regard to family pedigree.

sentences.zh: 公卿侍從，亦令舉勇力知謀之士，以備將材。

translations.literal: High ministers and attendants should also be ordered to recommend men of courage, strength, and stratagem, to supply material for generals.
translations.idiomatic: Grand ministers and court attendants should likewise be ordered to recommend men of courage, strength, and strategic mind, to build a pool of commanders.

sentences.zh: 庶搜羅既廣，禦侮有人。

translations.literal: Then if recruitment is broad enough, there will be men to repel insult.
translations.idiomatic: Cast the net wide enough, and there will always be men ready to repel the enemy.

sentences.zh: 昔者漢圖恢復，所恃者諸葛亮。

translations.literal: Formerly when Han sought restoration, it relied on Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Han sought to restore itself, it relied on Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 南宋禦金，所恃者張浚。

translations.literal: When the Southern Song resisted Jin, it relied on Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Song resisted the Jin, it relied on Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 彼皆忠義夙著，功業久立。

translations.literal: Both were long renowned for loyalty and righteousness, with achievements established for years.
translations.idiomatic: Both were long famed for loyalty and righteousness, with achievements established over many years.

sentences.zh: 及街亭一敗，亮辭丞相。

translations.literal: Yet after one defeat at Jieting, Liang resigned the post of Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after a single defeat at Jieting, Zhuge Liang stepped down as Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 符離未捷，浚解都督，何則？

translations.literal: When Fuli had not yet been won, Jun was relieved of supreme command — why?
translations.idiomatic: When Fuli had not yet been taken, Zhang Jun was stripped of supreme command—why?

sentences.zh: 賞罰明則將士奮也。

translations.literal: When rewards and punishments are clear, officers and soldiers are inspired.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards and punishments are clear, officers and soldiers fight with spirit.

sentences.zh: 昨德勝門下之戰，未聞摧陷強寇，但叠為勝負，互殺傷而已。

translations.literal: In yesterday's battle beneath Desheng Gate, there was no report of crushing the strong foe — only alternating victories and defeats, mutual slaughter and wounding.
translations.idiomatic: In the recent battle below Desheng Gate, no one crushed the enemy; the fighting merely seesawed back and forth, with casualties on both sides.

sentences.zh: 雖不足罰，亦不足賞。

translations.literal: Though insufficient to punish, also insufficient to reward.
translations.idiomatic: It warranted neither punishment nor reward.

sentences.zh: 乃石亨則自伯進侯，于謙則自二品遷一品。

translations.literal: Yet Shi Heng was promoted from earl to marquis, and Yu Qian moved from second rank to first.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shi Heng was promoted from earl to marquis, and Yu Qian advanced from the second to the first rank.

sentences.zh: 天下未聞其功，但見其賞，豈不怠忠臣義士之心乎？

translations.literal: Under Heaven their deeds have not been heard of, only their rewards seen — does this not dampen the hearts of loyal ministers and righteous men?
translations.idiomatic: The realm has heard nothing of their achievements, only of their rewards—does this not discourage loyal ministers and righteous men?

sentences.zh: 可令仍循舊秩，勿躐新階，他日勛名著而爵賞加，正未為晚。

translations.literal: They could be ordered to remain at their former ranks, not leap to new grades — when merit becomes famous on another day and titles and rewards are added, it would not yet be late.
translations.idiomatic: Let them keep their former ranks and not leap to new grades; when their merit is truly established, titles and rewards can follow—and it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 夫既與不忍奪者，姑息之政；

translations.literal: To both grant and be unwilling to take away is a policy of indulgence;
translations.idiomatic: To grant rewards yet be unwilling to withdraw them is a policy of indulgence;

sentences.zh: 既進不肯退者，患失之心。

translations.literal: to advance and refuse to retire is the mind of fearing loss.
translations.idiomatic: to advance yet refuse to step down is the mind of one who fears losing what he has gained.

sentences.zh: 上不行姑息之政，下不懷患失之心，則治平可計日而望也。

translations.literal: If above there is no indulgent policy and below no fear of loss, then good governance and peace can be counted on by the day.
translations.idiomatic: If indulgence is banished above and fear of loss below, good order and peace can be counted on within days.

sentences.zh: 向者御史建白，欲令大臣入內議政，疏寢不行。

translations.literal: Formerly a censor proposed that grand ministers enter the palace to deliberate on government; the memorial was shelved and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a censor proposed that senior ministers enter the palace to deliberate on policy, but the memorial was shelved and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 夫人主當總攬威權，親決機務。

translations.literal: The ruler should gather all authority in his hands and personally decide critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign should hold all authority in his own hands and personally decide matters of state.

sentences.zh: 政事早朝未決者，日禦便殿，使大臣敷奏。

translations.literal: Affairs undecided in the early morning court should be heard daily in the informal hall, with grand ministers presenting and reporting.
translations.idiomatic: When morning court leaves business unresolved, the Emperor should hold daily sessions in the informal hall and have senior ministers present their views.

sentences.zh: 言官察其邪正而糾劾之，史官直書簡冊，以示懲勸。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials should examine whether their words are upright or wicked and impeach them; historiographers should record directly in the annals, to show punishment and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials should scrutinize what is upright and what is corrupt and impeach accordingly; historiographers should record events plainly in the annals, to serve as warning and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 此前代故事，祖宗成法也，願陛下遵而行之。

translations.literal: These are precedents of former ages and established laws of our ancestors; we wish Your Majesty would follow and implement them.
translations.idiomatic: These are precedents of former dynasties and established laws of our ancestors; I pray Your Majesty will follow and enforce them.

sentences.zh: 若僅封章入奏，中旨外傳，恐偏聽獨任，致生奸亂，欲治化之成難矣。

translations.literal: If only sealed memorials are submitted and private edicts transmitted outward, I fear partial listening and sole decision-making will produce treachery and disorder, and the achievement of good governance will be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: If governance consists only of sealed memorials submitted inward and private edicts transmitted outward, I fear partial listening and unchecked authority will breed treachery and disorder, and good rule will be hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 人主之德，欲其明如日月以察直枉，仁如天地以覆群生，勇如雷霆以收威柄。

translations.literal: The virtues of a ruler should be: bright as sun and moon to discern the straight from the crooked, benevolent as Heaven and Earth to cover all living beings, brave as thunder to reclaim authority.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's virtue should be bright as sun and moon to distinguish right from wrong, benevolent as Heaven and Earth to shelter all living things, and bold as thunder to reclaim sovereign authority.

sentences.zh: 故司馬光之告君，以仁明武為言，即《中庸》所謂知仁勇也。

translations.literal: Thus when Sima Guang counseled the ruler, he spoke of benevolence, clarity, and martial resolve — that is what the Doctrine of the Mean calls wisdom, benevolence, and courage.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang counseled his ruler, he spoke of benevolence, clarity, and martial resolve—the very wisdom, benevolence, and courage described in the Doctrine of the Mean.

sentences.zh: 知仁勇非學而能之哉？

translations.literal: Can wisdom, benevolence, and courage be attained without study?
translations.idiomatic: Can wisdom, benevolence, and courage be acquired without study?

sentences.zh: 夫經莫要於《尚書》、《春秋》，史莫正於《通鑒綱目》。

translations.literal: Of the classics, none are more essential than the Documents and the Spring and Autumn; of histories, none more correct than the Comprehensive Mirror and Outlines.
translations.idiomatic: Among the classics, none are more essential than the Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals; among histories, none are more authoritative than the Comprehensive Mirror and its Outlines.

sentences.zh: 陛下留心垂覽。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should attend to them and peruse them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should devote attention to reading them.

sentences.zh: 其於君也，既知禹、湯、文、武之所以興，又知桀、紂、幽、厲之所以替，而趨避審矣。

translations.literal: In being a ruler, knowing both why Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu rose, and why Jie, Zhou, You, and Li fell, one's advance and retreat would be careful.
translations.idiomatic: As a ruler, knowing why Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu rose—and why Jie, Zhou, You, and Li fell—Your Majesty would know precisely what to pursue and what to avoid.

sentences.zh: 於馭內臣也，既知有呂強、張承業之忠，又知有仇士良、陳弘誌之惡；

translations.literal: In controlling inner eunuchs, knowing both the loyalty of Lü Qiang and Zhang Chengye, and the wickedness of Qiu Shiliang and Chen Hongzhi;
translations.idiomatic: In managing inner eunuchs, knowing the loyalty of Lü Qiang and Zhang Chengye as well as the wickedness of Qiu Shiliang and Chen Hongzhi;

sentences.zh: 於馭廷臣也，既知有蕭、曹、房、杜之良，又知有李林甫、楊國忠之奸，而用舍當矣。

translations.literal: in controlling court ministers, knowing both the good of Xiao, Cao, Fang, and Du, and the treachery of Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong — then employment and dismissal would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: in managing court ministers, knowing the worth of Xiao He, Cao Shen, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui as well as the treachery of Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong—then appointments and dismissals would be rightly made.

sentences.zh: 如是則於知仁勇之德，豈不大有助哉。

translations.literal: If so, would it not greatly assist the virtues of wisdom, benevolence, and courage?
translations.idiomatic: Would this not greatly strengthen the virtues of wisdom, benevolence, and courage?

sentences.zh: 茍徒如向者儒臣進講，誦述其善，諱避其惡，是猶恐道路之有陷阱，閉目而過之，其不至於冥行顛仆者幾何。

translations.literal: If mere Confucian ministers merely lecture as before, reciting the good and avoiding the evil, it is like fearing traps on the road and passing with eyes closed — how could one not stumble blindly?
translations.idiomatic: If Confucian lecturers merely recite the good and shun the evil, as in the past, it is like closing one's eyes for fear of traps on the road—how could one avoid stumbling blindly?

sentences.zh: 今天下雖遭大創，尚如金甌之未缺。

translations.literal: Today though the realm has suffered a great wound, it is still like a golden vessel not yet cracked.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm has suffered a grievous wound, it is still like a golden vessel not yet cracked.

sentences.zh: 誠能本聖學以見之政治，臣見國勢可強，仇恥可雪，兄弟之恩可全，祖宗之制可復，亦何憚而不為此。

translations.literal: If truly grounded in sage learning it were applied to governance, I see national strength can be restored, enemy shame avenged, fraternal bonds preserved, and ancestral institutions recovered — what is there to fear in doing this?
translations.idiomatic: If sage learning truly guided government, I see that national strength could be restored, national humiliation avenged, fraternal bonds preserved, and ancestral institutions revived—what is there to fear in acting?

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝優詔答之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; the Emperor answered with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 三年遷洗馬。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 也先使者乞遣報使，帝堅不許。

translations.literal: Esen's envoy begged that a return envoy be sent; the Emperor firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Esen's envoy requested that a return envoy be dispatched, but the Emperor firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 定之疏引故事以請，帝下廷議，竟不果遣。

translations.literal: Dingzhi memorialized citing precedent to request it; the Emperor referred it to court discussion, but in the end no envoy was sent.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhi memorialized citing precedent in support, but though the Emperor referred the matter to court discussion, no envoy was ultimately sent.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷右庶子。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to Right Sub-Reader.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Right Sub-Reader.

sentences.zh: 天順改元，調通政司左參議，仍兼侍講。

translations.literal: When the Tianshun reign title was adopted, he was transferred to Left Assistant Commissioner in the Office of Transmission, still concurrently serving as Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianshun reign was proclaimed, he was transferred to Left Assistant Commissioner in the Office of Transmission while retaining his post as Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 尋進翰林學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，進太常少卿，兼侍讀學士，直經筵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong acceded, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently Reader-in-Waiting, attending the Lectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong acceded, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently Reader-in-Waiting, and attended the imperial Lectures.

sentences.zh: 成化二年十二月，以本官入直文淵閣，進工部右侍郎，兼翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Chenghua, retaining his rank he entered duty at the Hall of Literary Deepness, was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works, concurrently Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Chenghua, he entered regular duty at the Hall of Literary Deepness, was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works, and retained his post as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 江西、湖廣災，有司方征民賦。

translations.literal: Jiangxi and Huguang suffered disasters; local authorities were just then levying taxes on the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi and Huguang were stricken by disaster, local authorities were still levying taxes on the people.

sentences.zh: 定之言國儲充積，倉庾至不能容。

translations.literal: Dingzhi said the state granaries were full to overflowing, storehouses could scarcely hold more.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhi observed that the state granaries were overflowing and the storehouses could hold no more.

sentences.zh: 而此張口待哺之氓，乃責其租課，非聖主恤下意。

translations.literal: Yet these people gaping and awaiting nourishment were still charged their rents and levies — this was not the compassionate intent of a sage ruler toward his subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these starving people were still being charged rent and levies—hardly the compassionate policy of a sage ruler toward his subjects.

sentences.zh: 帝感其言，即命停征。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved by his words and immediately ordered the levies halted.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his words, the Emperor immediately ordered the levies suspended.

sentences.zh: 四年進禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 萬貴妃專寵，皇后希得見，儲嗣未兆。

translations.literal: The Noble Consort Wan monopolized favor; the Empress rarely had audience; no heir was yet designated.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wan monopolized the Emperor's favor; the Empress was rarely granted audience; and no heir had yet been designated.

sentences.zh: 郕王女及笄未下嫁。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chu's daughter had reached marriageable age but had not been given in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chu's daughter had come of age but had not yet been given in marriage.

sentences.zh: 定之因久旱，並論及之。

translations.literal: Dingzhi, on the occasion of prolonged drought, addressed all these matters together.
translations.idiomatic: On the occasion of prolonged drought, Dingzhi addressed all these matters together in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 且請經筵兼講太祖禦制諸書，斥異端邪教，勿令害政耗財。

translations.literal: He also requested that the Lectures include the Hongwu Emperor's personally composed works, repudiate heterodox sects, and not let them harm government or drain the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the imperial Lectures include the Hongwu Emperor's personally composed works, repudiate heterodox cults, and prevent them from harming government and draining the treasury.

sentences.zh: 帝留其疏不下。

translations.literal: The Emperor kept his memorial without issuing a response.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor kept the memorial and issued no response.

sentences.zh: 五年卒官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，謚文安。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites with the posthumous name Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 定之謙恭質直，以文學名一時。

translations.literal: Dingzhi was modest, respectful, and plain-spoken, renowned in his time for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhi was modest, respectful, and plain-spoken, and was famed in his day for literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 嘗有中旨命制元宵詩，內使卻立以俟。

translations.literal: Once an imperial order commanded him to compose Lantern Festival poems; a eunuch stood back waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Once an imperial order commanded him to compose Lantern Festival poems, and a eunuch stood aside waiting.

sentences.zh: 據案伸紙，立成七言絕句百首。

translations.literal: Leaning on the desk he spread paper and instantly completed a hundred seven-character quatrains.
translations.idiomatic: He spread paper on the desk and on the spot completed a hundred seven-character quatrains.

sentences.zh: 又嘗一日草九制，筆不停書。

translations.literal: Again, on one occasion he drafted nine imperial edicts in a day, pen never pausing.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he drafted nine imperial edicts in a single day, his brush never pausing.

sentences.zh: 有質宋人名字者，就列其世次，若譜系然，人服其敏博。

translations.literal: When someone questioned him about Song dynasty names, he immediately listed their generations in order, like a genealogical chart — people admired his quickness and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: When someone tested him on Song-dynasty names, he immediately listed their generations in order like a genealogical chart, and people marveled at his quickness and erudition.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：英宗之復辟也，當師旅饑饉之余，民氣未復，權奸內訌，柱石傾移，朝野多故，時事亦孔棘矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When Emperor Yingzong restored the throne, it was amid the aftermath of armies and famine; popular spirit had not yet recovered; powerful traitors quarreled within; pillar-stones were toppled; court and countryside had many troubles — the times were exceedingly perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: When Emperor Yingzong restored the throne, the realm was still reeling from war and famine; popular morale had not recovered; powerful traitors feuded within; the pillars of state had been shaken; court and countryside were beset with troubles—the times were exceedingly perilous.

sentences.zh: 李賢以一身搘拄其間，沛然若有余。

translations.literal: Li Xian alone propped up affairs among them, abundant as if with surplus strength.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian alone bore up affairs in that crisis, with strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 獎厲人材，振飭綱紀。

translations.literal: He encouraged talent and restored discipline to law and custom.
translations.idiomatic: He encouraged talent and restored order to law and custom.

sentences.zh: 迨憲、孝之世，名臣相望，猶多賢所識拔。

translations.literal: By the reigns of Xian and Xiao, renowned ministers succeeded one another — many were men he had recognized and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: By the reigns of Xianzong and Xiaozong, renowned ministers succeeded one another—many of them men he had recognized and promoted.

sentences.zh: 偉哉宰相才也。

translations.literal: Magnificent — the talent of a prime minister!
translations.idiomatic: What grand talent for a prime minister!

sentences.zh: 彭時、商輅侃侃守義，盡忠獻納，粹然一出於正。

translations.literal: Peng Shi and Shang Lu spoke forthrightly and upheld righteousness, devoted in loyalty and offering counsel, purely and wholly from the upright path.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shi and Shang Lu spoke forthrightly and upheld righteousness, devoted in loyalty and frank in counsel, wholly grounded in the upright path.

sentences.zh: 其於慈懿典禮，非所謂善成君德者歟？

translations.literal: In the ritual affairs of Empress Dowager Ci and Empress Dowager Yi — are they not what is called those who well complete a ruler's virtue?
translations.idiomatic: In the ritual affairs of Empresses Dowager Ci and Yi, were they not precisely the sort of ministers who help complete a ruler's virtue?

sentences.zh: 輅科名與宋王曾、宋庠埒，德望亦無愧焉。

translations.literal: Lu's examination rank rivaled Song Wangzeng and Song Qi, and in virtue and reputation he had nothing to be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's examination standing rivaled that of Song Wangzeng and Song Qi, and in virtue and reputation he had nothing to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 呂原、嶽正、劉定之雖相業未優，而原之行誼，正之氣概，定之之建白，鹹有可稱，故以時次，並列於篇。

translations.literal: Though Lu Yuan, Yue Zheng, and Liu Dingzhi did not excel in prime ministerial achievement, Yuan's conduct and integrity, Zheng's spirit and bearing, and Dingzhi's memorial proposals all had points worth praising; therefore by chronological order they are listed together in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lu Yuan, Yue Zheng, and Liu Dingzhi did not rank among the greatest prime ministers, Yuan's conduct, Zheng's character, and Dingzhi's memorial proposals all had much to commend; therefore they are listed together here in chronological order.
